items.title: Go Church Belgium documentary: What viewers were not told about two former Lighthouse bishops
items.description: Two former bishops have criticised Dag Heward-Mills. But their earlier statements, legal histories and a disputed multimillion-dollar settlement figure deserve attention too. Lawrence Odonkor and Emmanuel Oko Mensah, both former Lighthouse bishops, and Dag Heward-Mills, the church’s founder. The Belgian documentary investigating Go Church has raised serious allegations concerning Bishop Dag Heward-Mills and Lighthouse Chapel International. Those claims deserve examination. So does the background of the people making them. Emmanuel Oko Mensah and Lawrence Odonkor once held senior positions in Lighthouse. Both now criticise its leadership. Here are three pieces of context viewers should consider before reaching conclusions. 1. Oko Mensah: Two strikingly different accounts In the documentary, Emmanuel Oko Mensah is asked whether he was brainwashed during his years in the church. He answers: “Absolutely. One hundred per cent.” He also says the pressure works because God, the church, and the pastor merge into one entity. Yet at his own consecration, he publicly thanked Dag Heward-Mills for being a patient father and for giving him opportunities. He said: “Bishop has been so good to me.” He also thanked Dag Heward-Mills for giving a chance to people he described as flawed and unqualified, including himself. What changed between those two accounts? Earlier praise does not automatically disprove later criticism — and a man who says he was brainwashed would expect to have felt grateful at the time. But the public should hear both statements, in context, and ask what explains the difference. The same man, years apart. Left: at his consecration. Right: in the Belgian documentary. 2. Larry Odonkor: The legal record matters Lawrence “Larry” Odonkor alleges that problems within Lighthouse came from the top. His own legal history is also relevant background. He is also the source of the harshest language in the programme. He says that if the devil walks the earth in the form of a human being, that is Mills; that he uses his brilliance to do evil; and that it is not about God at all, but about fame and money. In April 2023, a court in Antananarivo, Madagascar, convicted him of breach of trust in proceedings concerning church funds and property. The judgment was delivered in his absence; it imposed a two-year prison sentence and 75 million Malagasy Ariary in damages. A December 2025 Ghana News Agency report said appeals had been dismissed in May 2024 and November 2025. Odonkor disputed the judgment. In a separate Ghanaian case, an Accra Circuit Court acquitted him in September 2023, finding dishonest appropriation had not been established. The Attorney-General subsequently challenged that decision on appeal. These are separate cases with different outcomes. Neither the Madagascar conviction nor the Ghanaian acquittal settles the truth of Odonkor’s allegations about Dag Heward-Mills. Readers should be given the full legal context. Watch: “Larry Odonkor convicted for fraud” (UDVerse) 3. The $12 million settlement controversy In 2021, reports emerged about a $12 million figure discussed in a dispute involving six former Lighthouse pastors, including Oko Mensah and Odonkor. Lighthouse’s lawyers alleged the former pastors had demanded that amount. Their lawyer denied making a formal demand; a mediator said the figure arose during settlement discussions as a possible calculation, not a formal demand. That distinction matters. It would be inaccurate to state as an established fact that the men demanded $12 million or that money explains their later criticism. What is clear from the reporting is that a significant financial dispute formed part of the wider history. Separately, a 2021 SSNIT determination was reported as largely supporting Lighthouse’s position on pension contributions, with one month’s contribution outstanding for Oko Mensah. That finding, and the former pastors’ objections, should be considered together. A settlement letter of 16 December 2022 set the claim out person by person, under four headings, with a sub-total for each man and then a second figure four times larger. Name Years Underpayment Compensation Severance and resettlement Sub-total Luke 19:8 total Faith Makafui Fiakojo 6 25,200 3,400 125,000 178,800 715,200 Edem Amankwah 9 39,600 195,100 181,000 455,300 1,821,200 Seth Duncan 10 62,400 7,100 271,000 402,900 1,611,600 Edward Laryea 12 58,800 79,216 287,400 484,216 1,936,864 Emmanuel Oko-Mensah 17 — 25,630 519,750 545,380 2,181,520 Lawrence Odonkor 19 14,400 385,400 579,600 993,800 3,975,200 TOTAL 3,060,396 12,241,584 All figures in US dollars, payable in cedis. Pension contributions are not costed, only marked for update. Fees are stated as ten per cent of whatever is paid. The itemised claim — underpayment, compensation, severance and resettlement — comes to about $3.06 million. The $12.24 million appears only in the final column, after a fourfold multiplier drawn from Luke 19:8, in which Zacchaeus the tax collector offers to restore fourfold anything he has taken. Every line is exactly four times its own sub-total. The largest single claim is Lawrence Odonkor’s, at nearly $4 million — almost twice the next man’s, and roughly a third of the whole figure. What about Dag Heward-Mills and Go Church? Go Church Belgium has publicly disputed allegations about its practices and has said donations are voluntary. Its responses deserve to be examined alongside the documentary’s claims, rather than left out of the conversation. When relationships break down, memories and interpretations can change. But a falling-out does not erase genuine kindness, just as earlier gratitude does not rule out later grievances. That is why the recordings, court decisions, financial dispute and the church’s response should all be available to readers. Watch the videos. Read the records. Hear the response. Then decide for yourself.

items.title: LFR 2026: Le Premier ministre interpelle les députés, «ne punissez pas le Peuple !»
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô a mis en garde contre les conséquences d’un rejet du projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026, sur les entreprises du bâtiment et des travaux publics (BTP), les travailleurs et les ménages. Lors de la conférence de presse du gouvernement sur le projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026, tenue le 25 octobre à Dakar, le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô a appelé à l’adoption du texte, mettant en avant ses conséquences économiques et sociales. «Ne punissez pas le peuple !», a-t-il dit aux députés, défendant la nécessité d’adapter les équilibres budgétaires aux évolutions intervenues, depuis l’adoption de la loi de finances initiale. Le chef du gouvernement a également mis en garde contre les conséquences d’un rejet de la LFR pour les entreprises du bâtiment et des travaux publics (BTP), confrontées à des difficultés de trésorerie et à l’interruption de certains chantiers. «Ne pas voter la LFR, c’est empêcher des entreprises du bâtiment et des travaux publics de retrouver de la trésorerie, de reprendre des chantiers interrompus, de payer leurs fournisseurs et de renouveler leurs équipements», a-t-il dit. Selon toujours le Premier ministre, «c’est empêcher des ouvriers, des techniciens, des ingénieurs et des cadres de travailler et de percevoir leurs salaires. C’est empêcher des familles de régler leur loyer et de faire face à leurs dépenses scolaires», a affirmé Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô.

items.title: Billionaire Trump backer Bill Ackman says Ben-Gvir, Smotrich should not serve in next Israeli govt
items.description: Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman on Sunday said that Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel’s next government, saying the two far-right politicians had caused enormous damage to the country’s reputation. The public intervention by the prominent hedge fund manager, who is Jewish, comes just two days before Israel’s general election, in which polls show a tight race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition and the opposition. Ackman wrote on X that from the perspective of someone who had an understanding of how Israel was perceived in the United States, “Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions”. The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, who praised Netanyahu last week, said a government without the two ministers would send a message that Israel was “turning a new page”. “This will allow Israel to rebuild lost credibility, increase the opportunity for an expansion of the Abraham Accords, and enjoy a better relationship with Democrats and Republicans and Americans at large,” he said. The Abraham Accords are the 2020 agreement, mediated by US President Donald Trump’s first administration, that saw Israel establish relations with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. It later re-established official ties with Morocco. Representatives for Ben-Gvir and Smotrich did not immediately respond to requests for comment. As ministers in Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have overseen policies widely perceived as discriminatory against Israel’s minority Arab population and Palestinians living in the occupied West Bank. Several countries, including Britain, Canada and Australia, have imposed sanctions on the two ministers over accusations that they have incited violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 parliamentary seats at Tuesday’s election, up from 6, while Smotrich’s Religious Zionism is projected to win 8, up from 7. Ackman, who was visiting Israel last week, and who along with his wife Neri Oxman owns 5 per cent of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, supported Trump’s candidacy for president in 2024. Trump last week publicly endorsed Netanyahu for prime minister. Nimrod Goren, the president of Israeli think tank Mitvim, said Ackman’s statement appeared to reflect a desire among Trump’s circles for Netanyahu to drop his far-right allies after the vote to form a ‘unity government’ with opposition parties. However, Gadi Eisenkot, the leading challenger to Netanyahu, and other opposition party leaders have ruled out forming a government with Israel’s longest-serving prime minister. Speaking at a Tel Aviv conference on Thursday, Ackman praised Netanyahu, who he said had done a good job in protecting and defending Israel since the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Thousands of Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday, calling for an independent inquiry into the attack that killed around 1,200 people.

items.title: 2027: NDC slams Tinubu, APC over ₦1bn worth of Prado SUVs for youth leaders
items.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) after its National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, announced the distribution of brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs to selected youth leaders for election mobilisation. The NDC said the seven vehicles shown in a video posted by Israel were worth about ₦1.015bn, accusing the ruling party of spending taxpayers’ money on the lavish lifestyles of politicians while Nigerians grapple with economic hardship. The average cost of a brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado is ₦145,000,000. In this video, we counted seven such vehicles, and the number could be even higher. The total cost of these seven vehicles alone amounts to ₦1,015,000,000. While the rudderless, clueless, and ruinous… https://t.co/QYeB7UU21y — Nigeria Democratic Congress (@NigeriaNDCHQ) October 25, 2026 In a post on X reacting to Israel’s video, the opposition party said the estimated cost of the vehicles reflected what it described as wasteful spending by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration. “The average cost of a brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado is ₦145,000,000. In this video, we counted seven such vehicles, and the number could be even higher,” the NDC said. “The total cost of these seven vehicles alone amounts to ₦1,015,000,000.” The party criticised the government’s economic policies, saying Nigerians had been asked to endure hardship while political leaders continued to enjoy expensive benefits. “While the rudderless, clueless, and ruinous administration of President Bola Tinubu has been asking Nigerians to endure the pains of its wicked and cruel reforms, this is how taxpayers’ money is being spent,” it said. “The wasteful APC-led administration is funding the lavish lifestyles of politicians while ordinary Nigerians wallow in poverty.” The NDC called on Nigerians to vote the ruling party out in the 2027 general election, describing opposition to the administration as a civic responsibility. “We cannot continue like this. We owe Nigerians and the unborn generation the civic duty to vote the ruinous administration of President Bola Tinubu out of power,” the party said. It also used the controversy to promote its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, pledging that his administration would reduce the cost of governance. “Our presidential candidate is strongly committed to cutting the cost of governance,” the NDC said, urging voters to support Obi for what it described as “a new and working Nigeria for all, and not for a corrupt few”. Israel had earlier posted a video showing the vehicles, saying they were presented to selected youth leaders to support their election mobilisation activities. “Today, I presented brand new 2026 Prado to my committed selected youth leaders to aid their election mobilisation activities,” he wrote. He also thanked First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for her support for the party’s structure under his leadership. “I am grateful to my Mummy, H.E Mrs Oluremi Tinubu for her continuous support to the party structure under my leadership,” Israel said. He added that the APC would focus on grassroots mobilisation ahead of the election, saying the party would “deliver polling unit by polling unit”. The NDC’s valuation is based on its estimate of the vehicles’ average price and its count of seven SUVs in the video. items.title: Flights resume at Riyadh airport as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
items.description: Flights resumed at Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday following a series of deadly attacks on the facility that saw it closed for two weeks, even as Yemen’s Houthis targeted the country with strikes. King Khalid International Airport’s website showed several domestic and international flights scheduled on Sunday, including arrivals to the kingdom from Dubai, Paris and Cairo. The renewed operations at the airport came as explosions rattled Riyadh early Sunday, after a text message was sent to residents warning of a hostile threat targeting the city. The airport closure was a major blow for Saudi Arabia, with the kingdom’s flagship investment conference postponed until 2027 as residents scrambled to find alternatives to enter and exit the country. The prestigious motor sport race, the Dakar Rally, also added its name to a long list of events to be cancelled, postponed or relocated amid the fallout from the war. Saudi officials did not provide additional information when asked by AFP about the scope of the renewed operations at the airport. But the tracking website Flightradar24 showed a small number of flights had departed, though the vast majority were cancelled. The Houthis have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree earlier warned that Riyadh airport was still “unsafe” and a “military target”. “The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines — as well as staff and travellers — against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces,” he said. “The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport.” – ‘Everything is shaking’ – Later on Sunday, Saree said Saudi Arabia had struck Yemen dozens of times over the previous 24 hours. “During the past 24 hours, Saudi warplanes launched 56 airstrikes and missiles targeting civilian objects in the governorates of Hajjah, Lahj, Amran, Saada, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Ibb using F-15 and “Typhoon” planes that took off from the bases of Khamis Mushait and Taif, and missiles from Najran,” he said on X. As operations at the airport restarted, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis arrived in Riyadh and met with Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. During the meeting, Mitsotakis “responded favourably to the kingdom’s request to keep the Patriot system in Saudi Arabia, given the current challenging circumstances”, his office said. Greece has deployed a battery to operate the US-made Patriot air defence system in Yanbu, a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast. The SPA news agency added that the two leaders “underscored the critical importance of safeguarding the security and integrity of international maritime corridors and ensuring the safe and continuous flow of energy supplies to global markets”. Earlier, the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted at least 10 ballistic missiles. The fighting erupted after a years-long truce between the Houthis and Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government fell apart. “The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning — may God keep us safe. Everything is shaking because of the explosions,” one resident in Khamis Mushait told AFP on Sunday on condition of anonymity. The kingdom’s civil defence agency later said two people were injured in the south by falling debris, also reporting damage to several buildings and vehicles. Images released by the official Saudi Press Agency showed a building with part of its upper facade destroyed, exposing metal rods. Another image captured large windows shattered, with shards of glass strewn across the pavement and part of the road. – Attack warning – AFP journalists in Riyadh heard three explosions in the early hours of Sunday, with residents receiving alert messages for a “hostile aerial threat” and urging them to stay in a safe place. The warning came as the Saudi-led coalition said it had downed a ballistic missile launched by the group towards the capital, as well as two drones in the Riyadh area. “Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh,” the coalition posted on X. Later Sunday morning, the coalition said its forces intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southern city of Khamis Mushait. Attacks appeared to target areas across the south, with warnings also issued for Abha city along with areas in Taif, Namas and Jazan. The attacks came after the Houthis said they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base within 24 hours. items.title: 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations
items.description: By Dickson Omobola President Bola Tinubu has appointed Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, to head the Directorate of Air Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 re-election campaign Keyamo would serve as Director of the Directorate of Air Mobilisation, with the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, Mrs Olubunmi Kuku, appointed Deputy Director 1, while Engr Farouk Ahmed Umar would serve as Deputy Director II. Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, Tunde Moshood, in a statement, said the appointments underscored the strategic importance of air transportation, operational coordination and aviation logistics to the organisation of a nationwide presidential campaign in a country as geographically extensive as Nigeria. The statement reads: ‘The Directorate of Air Mobilisation is expected to play a crucial role in coordinating the campaign’s air-movement requirements, facilitating travel arrangements for designated campaign officials and personnel, and ensuring effective planning for air transportation in support of campaign activities across the six geopolitical zones of the country. “Given the scale of the 2027 presidential campaign, the directorate is expected to work closely with other relevant campaign structures to promote seamless coordination, operational efficiency and effective deployment of available logistical resources, subject to applicable aviation regulations and electoral laws. “Keyamo’s appointment brings to the campaign structure the experience of a serving aviation minister who has been at the forefront of policy initiatives aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s aviation sector, improving its international standing and positioning the country as a major aviation hub in Africa. “His familiarity with the operational demands of the aviation industry is expected to provide useful leadership in coordinating the directorate’s activities and establishing an effective framework for air-mobilisation planning. “The appointment of Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku and Umar as Deputy Directors also brings aviation-sector leadership and technical experience into the directorate, strengthening its capacity to address the planning and coordination demands associated with nationwide campaign movements.” The post 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NACOC Director-General urges journalists to investigate drug trafficking networks in Ghana
items.description: The Director-General of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey, has challenged journalists to investigate the networks and vulnerabilities that enable drug trafficking rather than focusing mainly on arrests and drug seizures. He said deeper media investigations into how trafficking networks operate and the gaps they exploit could improve public understanding of the narcotics trade and strengthen efforts to protect vulnerable communities. The Ashanti Regional Director of NACOC, Rees Hakeem Oduro, delivered the message on behalf of the Director-General at the Ashanti Media Excellence Awards in Kumasi. He urged journalists to look beyond dramatic headlines and examine the wider issues surrounding narcotics, including institutional responses and measures needed to safeguard communities. “When the public hears about a drug seizure or an arrest, there is an understandable interest in the immediate facts. But there is also a wider story,” he said. Major General Mantey encouraged journalists to use their platforms to highlight community concerns, particularly those affecting young people and other vulnerable groups. He also stressed the need for evidence-based reporting on narcotics cases, warning journalists against presenting allegations as established facts. The Director-General said NACOC remained committed to constructive engagement with the media to promote public education, accountability and efforts to protect society from the harms associated with illicit drugs. The remarks were delivered under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Championing Credibility: Journalism in the Age of AI.”

items.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 : Mbappé, Lamine Yamal et Harry Kane au coude-à-coude avant le verdict
items.description: La cérémonie du Ballon d’Or se tient lundi à Londres, avec une course particulièrement disputée entre Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal et Harry Kane. Chez les femmes, l’absence d’Aitana Bonmatí ouvre la voie à une possible troisième consécration d’Alexia Putellas. Le suspense est à son comble avant la remise du Ballon d’Or 2026. Pour sa 70e édition, la prestigieuse récompense individuelle sera décernée lundi à Londres, une première pour la cérémonie organisée par France Football au Royaume-Uni. Trois noms dominent les débats : le Français Kylian Mbappé, l’Espagnol Lamine Yamal et l’Anglais Harry Kane, tous trois portés par une saison remarquable. Le trophée désignera le successeur d’Ousmane Dembélé. Malgré la conservation de son titre en Ligue des champions, l’attaquant français n’a pas retrouvé, sur le plan individuel, l’éclat qui avait marqué sa précédente saison. Une situation qui laisse la porte ouverte à une lutte particulièrement serrée. Sur le plan statistique, Harry Kane affiche un bilan exceptionnel. L’attaquant du Bayern Munich a inscrit 61 buts avec son club, qui a atteint les demi-finales de la compétition européenne. En ajoutant ses réalisations avec l’équipe d’Angleterre, troisième de la Coupe du monde 2026, son total grimpe à 73 buts. Seul Lionel Messi a fait mieux sur une saison, avec 82 réalisations en 2010-2011. À 33 ans, le capitaine des Three Lions affirme toutefois vouloir éviter de se laisser absorber par la course au trophée. Après le match nul 2-2 contre Arsenal, mercredi, il a reconnu qu’il était difficile de ne pas y penser, tout en espérant profiter pleinement de la cérémonie. Cette approche contraste avec celle de ses deux principaux concurrents, qui ont affiché plus directement leurs ambitions. Lamine Yamal revendique sa place parmi les favoris À 19 ans, Lamine Yamal n’a pas caché sa confiance. L’ailier du FC Barcelone estime mériter le Ballon d’Or au regard de ses performances et des titres remportés, notamment en championnat d’Espagne et à la Coupe du monde. Le jeune international espagnol considère également que lui et Kylian Mbappé sont les deux meilleurs joueurs du monde, une déclaration qui illustre sa détermination à s’imposer au sommet du football mondial. De son côté, le Français de 27 ans peut faire valoir des statistiques individuelles particulièrement solides, malgré l’absence de trophée collectif cette saison. Il a terminé meilleur buteur du championnat espagnol avec 25 réalisations et de la Ligue des champions avec 15 buts. Il est également devenu le meilleur buteur de l’histoire de la Coupe du monde, avec 22 réalisations, dont dix inscrites lors de l’édition 2026. « J’ai été meilleur buteur dans les plus grandes compétitions », a souligné Mbappé, qui se dit optimiste quant à ses chances de remporter la récompense. Entre les statistiques du Français, les titres et l’ambition du jeune Espagnol, et l’efficacité offensive de Kane, le choix des votants s’annonce particulièrement difficile. Comment est attribué le Ballon d’Or ? Le Ballon d’Or est attribué à l’issue d’un vote de journalistes, avec un représentant par pays parmi les 100 premières nations du classement masculin de la FIFA et les 50 premières du classement féminin. Les critères de sélection sont hiérarchisés : les performances individuelles et l’influence du joueur sur les résultats arrivent en premier, suivies des performances collectives et des trophées remportés. Le comportement sportif constitue le troisième critère. La liste des 30 candidats comprend plusieurs autres grandes figures du football, parmi lesquelles l’Espagnol Rodri, son compatriote Fabián Ruiz, le Géorgien Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, l’Argentin Lionel Messi, déjà huit fois récompensé, ainsi que le Français Michael Olise. Ce dernier a réalisé une saison remarquable avec le Bayern Munich, avec 31 passes décisives et 22 buts selon les chiffres cités dans la présentation des candidats. Chez les femmes, Alexia Putellas vise une troisième couronne La course au Ballon d’Or féminin est elle aussi marquée par une incertitude majeure : l’absence d’Aitana Bonmatí. La milieu de terrain espagnole, récompensée trois années consécutives de 2023 à 2025, a été freinée par des blessures qui ont perturbé sa saison 2025-2026. Cette situation offre une occasion à Alexia Putellas de retrouver le sommet. Déjà sacrée en 2021 et 2022, l’Espagnole peut décrocher un troisième Ballon d’Or, un exploit qu’elle partagerait avec sa compatriote Bonmatí. Ancienne joueuse du FC Barcelone et désormais sous les couleurs de London City Lionesses, Putellas devra notamment faire face à la concurrence de la Polonaise Ewa Pajor et de l’Espagnole Claudia Pina, ses anciennes coéquipières au sein du club catalan. La liste des prétendantes comprend également la milieu haïtienne Melchie Dumornay, qui évolue à Lyon, et l’attaquante jamaïcaine Khadija Shaw, joueuse de Manchester City. Plusieurs récompenses au programme La cérémonie de lundi, présentée notamment par l’ancien international français Thierry Henry, sera également l’occasion de remettre plusieurs autres distinctions, dont celles du meilleur entraîneur, du meilleur jeune joueur et du meilleur gardien de but. Une nouvelle récompense fera par ailleurs son apparition : le « Ballon d’Or du meilleur de tous les temps ». Elle sera attribuée à une ancienne gloire ayant remporté le Ballon d’Or au moins deux fois, sur la base d’un vote électronique ouvert au public. Entre la bataille à trois chez les hommes, l’ouverture de la course féminine et l’arrivée de cette nouvelle distinction, la cérémonie londonienne s’annonce comme un rendez-vous majeur pour le football mondial. items.title: JoyNews’ Nana Boakye Yiadom wins Community Impact Journalism Award; two others at Ashanti GJA Awards
items.description: JoyNews journalist Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom has won the Best in Community Impact Journalism award at the 2025 Ashanti Regional Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Awards, alongside two other recognitions for his work in environmental and health journalism. He won the top award with his investigative documentary, Deadly Doses – Unmasking Ghana’s Drug Epidemic, which examined the growing challenge of substance abuse and its devastating effects on individuals and communities. The documentary explored the realities of drug use, particularly among young people, highlighting the social and health consequences of addiction while drawing attention to the need for effective interventions. Nana Boakye also placed second in the Best in Environment, Science and Climate Journalism category with his feature, Greens to Pit, which focused on the destruction of the cocoa farms through illegal mining. He secured third place in the Health Journalism category with his feature, A Sick Hospital, which examined challenges confronting healthcare delivery at the Tafo government hospital in Kumasi. The three recognitions underscore his reporting on critical social, environmental and public health issues, with a focus on stories that highlight community concerns and promote public accountability. His award-winning works were produced for JoyNews and Luv FM.

items.title: Learn leadership from Macron amid killings, hardship – ADC to Tinubu
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) on Sunday challenged President Bola Tinubu to learn from French President Emmanuel Macron, accusing him of failing to show sufficient empathy for Nigerians grappling with insecurity, hunger and economic hardship. The council said the reported postponement of Macron’s scheduled state visit to Nigeria underscored the need for leaders to pay attention to pressing domestic challenges, arguing that Nigerians facing killings, mass abductions and rising living costs deserve more visible concern from their president. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC cited reports that Macron had rescheduled his October 28–29, 2026 visit to Nigeria, including the planned France-Nigeria Business Forum in Lagos, to early 2027 amid domestic challenges in France. “A president will not travel when his home is contending with internal combustion,” a Nigerian official familiar with the development was quoted as saying. The ADC-PCC said the welfare of citizens should remain central to governance, citing attacks and killings in Plateau, Niger, Benue, Zamfara, Kaduna, Kogi, Kwara, Katsina, Sokoto and other parts of the country. It also raised concerns over a reported incident in Niger State involving the detention of more than 60 young Nigerians under allegedly inhumane conditions, with over 37 reportedly dying in custody. Describing the incident as a grave national concern, the council demanded urgent government intervention, accountability and justice for the affected families. It faulted Tinubu’s response, claiming that Vice President Kashim Shettima visited the state weeks after the incident, following a visit by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to commiserate with affected communities and bereaved families. The council said Atiku’s visit demonstrated the importance of identifying with citizens in moments of grief, arguing that public office holders must show concern through direct engagement with affected people, not merely official statements. “President Macron has offered a reminder that the concerns of citizens must remain central to leadership. When a country faces a serious domestic crisis, its leadership must demonstrate urgency, compassion and a willingness to take responsibility,” the council said. The ADC-PCC urged the Tinubu administration to prioritise the protection of lives, tackle insecurity and ease the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It also demanded answers over deaths in custody and alleged unlawful detention, insisting that affected families deserved justice and those responsible should be held accountable. The post Learn leadership from Macron amid killings, hardship – ADC to Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: MMDAs directed to maintain Nissan Patrol vehicles for Traditional Councils
items.description: The Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs has directed Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) in possession of Nissan Patrol four-wheel-drive vehicles to maintain them in good working condition for use by Traditional Councils within their respective jurisdictions. In a directive dated October 22, the Chief Director, Amin Abdul-Rahaman, said the Minister had instructed the Assemblies to ensure the vehicles were maintained to facilitate traditional authorities’ official movements and engagements. “In recognition of the important role of Traditional Councils in local governance, customary administration, dispute resolution, community mobilisation and development, appropriate logistical arrangements must be made to facilitate their official movements,” the directive stated. The Assemblies have been instructed to establish administrative arrangements to facilitate the use of the vehicles for official travel and other authorised engagements, subject to agreed scheduling and accountability procedures. They are also expected to make budgetary and logistical provisions for routine servicing, insurance and other essential operating costs, in line with applicable financial and procurement regulations. The directive explicitly prohibits the Assemblies from selling or transferring the vehicles, stressing that “no Assembly shall auction, dispose of, transfer or otherwise alienate its existing Nissan Patrol four-wheel-drive vehicles.” It added that the vehicles “are to be preserved, repaired where necessary and maintained for the intended purpose of facilitating official travel by Traditional Councils”, unless otherwise authorised in writing by the appropriate competent authority in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The Ministry has directed all MMDAs to give the matter priority and ensure that their administrative, transport and finance units take immediate steps to implement the directive. “Regional Ministers are requested to monitor compliance by Assemblies within their respective regions,” the letter stated, adding that the directive should be treated as urgent and for immediate compliance.

items.title: 2027: PDP meets INEC deadline on omitted candidates
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, has met the Independent National Electoral Commission’s, INEC, October 24 deadline for correcting the names of candidates omitted from its published list, the party’s National Organising Secretary, Captain Umar Bature (rtd), has said. The affected candidates include governorship hopefuls in Gombe and Ogun states, as well as about six or seven House of Assembly candidates, whose names were missing from the list released by the electoral commission. Bature confirmed the development on Sunday in a response to Vanguard, saying the party had completed the corrections within the stipulated period. “Yes, we met the deadline since,” he said. He said the omissions involved candidates contesting governorship elections in the two states and several House of Assembly seats. items.title: NCCIA says child pornography network busted, with father allegedly involved in selling videos of his children
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Sunday claimed to have busted an international child pornography network in which a father was allegedly involved in making and selling explicit videos of his own children. Islamabad NCCIA Additional Director Mohammad Shoaib Khan, speaking at a press conference in the capital, asserted that this was the first case in Pakistan’s history where a father was found involved in such a heinous crime against his own minor children. The NCCIA official claimed the man was “involved in making indecent videos of his children, aged between four and five, and selling them”. The videos were bought and sold in secret Telegram groups through cryptocurrency, he added. Khan added the investigation also revealed disturbing scenes of animal abuse in the videos. He said the alleged ringleader of the gang belonged to Skardu and was arrested with the assistance of international agencies. During the investigation, important links and evidence were recovered from Islamabad, Multan and South Punjab, and raids were being conducted to arrest other network facilitators, according to Khan. “Those involved in such heinous crimes will be brought to justice,” the NCCIA official declared. Recalling another case, Khan said the agency arrested four members of an alleged child pornography gang after investigating around 60 videos recovered from a child’s mobile phone. He said the suspect used to befriend children aged between six and 14 on Instagram, lure them with money and make indecent videos, which were then sold internationally via WhatsApp groups. Khan claimed that two Chinese nationals had also been convicted earlier in this crime. Sharing details of another case, the additional director said a minor girl from Karachi attempted suicide after being fed up with harassment. The girl is currently under treatment at a hospital, he added. Khan claimed the NCCIA team, with the help of the victim’s family, traced and arrested the main suspect from Islamabad in just 13 hours. He added that the suspect had allegedly been harassing and blackmailing the victim for the last two to three years. “Providing justice to the affected families is our top priority. Strict implementation of a zero-tolerance policy against those harassing women and children is being ensured,” he said. The additional director further advised social media users to remain vigilant. “Think before uploading any indecent material. The law is in action; those uploading wrong content will not escape the law in any case,” he said. He urged citizens not to share their one-time password, bank account details or personal information with anyone and to beware of fake numbers on fake websites, as calling them may lead to emptying of accounts. “If you are a victim of cybercrime, do not remain silent; NCCIA stands with you,” he said, adding that citizens can call helpline 1799 for complaints, which is available 24 hours. ‘Zero-tolerance’ policy against cyber harassment of women, children According to a separate statement issued by the NCCIA, the agency’s Director General (DG) Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi directed adopting a zero-tolerance policy against “elements harassing citizens,” particularly women and children, on social media. The directions were made in a meeting attended by Khan, Director IT Atif Abbas, in-charge of social media Tayyaba Daulat, Public Relations Officer Mehboob Elahi, among others. The meeting, per the statement, was given a detailed briefing on social media monitoring, prevention of fake news, cyber harassment cases, public awareness campaign and digital handling of cybercrime complaints. “DG NCCIA issued directions to make citizens’ protection on social media, prompt redressal of complaints and institutional coordination more effective and active,” it said. The DG further ordered strict monitoring of accounts spreading fake news, negative propaganda against state institutions and fear and panic among the public, and indiscriminate action against those responsible, according to the statement. On October 23, NCCIA Karachi Zone claimed to have arrested suspects from three firms allegedly involved in production, promotion, and online sale of sexually explicit animated cartoons, animated child sexual abuse material, pornographic digital content and other digital designing services to international customers. A recent Unicef report revealed that an estimated 1.5 million children in Pakistan experienced online sexual abuse in one year. As per the report, around 85 per cent of perpetrators were known to the victims, aged between 12 and 17. Furthermore, 71pc of victims did not tell anyone, according to the Unicef report, while no child surveyed reported the abuse through formal channels — including police, helplines or social workers. Meanwhile, child protection NGO Sahil estimates that at least 1,914 cases of child abuse were reported across the country in the first six months of 2026. From January to June 2026, as many as 1,015 cases of child sexual abuse, 558 cases of abduction, 101 cases of missing children and 35 cases of child marriage were reported. Further, 98 cases of pornography following sexual abuse were also recorded. The Sahil report was compiled on the basis of data collected from different national and regional newspapers of all four provinces, including Islamabad Capital Territory, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan. Of the total reported cases, 58 per cent of victims were girls. The data also showed that children aged 11-15 years were the most vulnerable to abuse.

items.title: Bright Simons proposes $13m civil service AI assistant as alternative to Ghana’s $270m GhanaChat plan
items.description: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons has proposed a cheaper alternative to Ghana’s planned US$270 million GhanaChat project, arguing that a sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) assistant for the civil service could be a more practical starting point for the country’s AI ambitions. In a post on X, Mr Simons questioned the rationale for developing a national AI platform to compete with global services such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude when existing models could potentially support government operations at a lower cost. 1. Readers of this page know by now that JoyNews held a forum on Ghana’s AI strategy and prospects. And the Digital Minister and I got into a serious debate about his Ministry’s plan to build Ghana’s competitor to Gemini, Kimi, ChatGPT, Qwen, Claude, etc. 2. Ghana’s competitor to these global AI platforms is called GhanaChat. 3. It will be trained and hosted in a brand new AI datacenter. 4. 48 registries pooling data from across the public sector will make this AI smarter about Ghana than the foreign ones. 5. The AI datacenter and the "AI Fund" will cost about $270 million. Expect more to be spent on the registries and the apps. A lot of contracts. You can bet that a lot of ICT contractors are very happy. 6. The question is, if we have a couple of hundred million dollars to spend on making AI deliver great benefits for Ghana, should we spend it on GhanaChat, a top-tier AI data center, and the data-pooling system? And should we do it according to the strategy the Ministry has devised? 7. Or could we do much better by more critically assessing all our strategic options and comparing them to the Ministry’s? 8. My argument on the show was that I am not convinced about GhanaChat offering the best value for our money. 9. It would take many pages to explain my position fully. But in this post I will highlight just the most important points. 10. Attached are extracts from page 13, 50, and 68 of Ghana’s AI strategy. 11. If you have even the barest exposure to AI, you can see a massive error. Can you? 12. The target for how much computing capacity the country needs for next year (2027) is indicated as "1021 FLOPS" and the 2035 target as "1025 FLOPS". 13. If this was indeed correct, it would mean that the Ministry would like the entire computing capacity of the country in 2027 to be equivalent to a 1970s desktop computer. Or 2% of the capacity of the 1980 Intel math chip. 14. Howzat? 15. I’m sure you can agree that this would be totally ridiculous if that was the Ministry’s intent. So, what happened? 16. Somebody who didn’t fully understand how FLOPS work must have been involved in the drafting. What was meant to be 10 raised to the power 21 operations per second (10²¹ operations a second) was written out as "1021". Same for "1025". 17. Why wasn’t the error caught? Because in Ghana when doing "consultations", governments rarely engage independent and critical voices who will point out absurdities without fear of offending big men and women. 18. I am not being petty. There is a serious strategic confusion beyond mere typos. 19. Read properly as 10²¹ FLOPS, the Ministry is telling us that by next year it will have some 200,000 of Nvidia’s newest chips in use in Ghana, 500 MW of power devoted to AI, all costing about US$24 billion (close to the Ghanaian government’s entire programmed spending for 2026). 20. The US$250 million AI datacenter now being procured supplies about 1% of this 2027 target. 21. Howzat? 22. Clearly, no serious critique of the plan would have okayed such a vision. Throughout the ministry’s own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged. 23. My first major point here is that this is classic KATANOMICS: the lack of critical policy audiences. This is exactly how a sugar factory that was "designed from the start to fail" was allowed to be built. Many programs and initiatives in Ghana fail for precisely this absence of critical review. 24. In the strategy, you find statements like: "government aggressively building AI compute clusters" and by courting hyperscalers, "to leverage the scaling laws towards building general purpose AI and AGI". Then: "drastically increase Ghana’s energy capacity 0.5 to 1 OOM per year". "OOM" means "order of magnitude". 25. When I challenged the Minister on TV, he confidently rebutted by claiming that the Energy Minister/Ministry has assured him of feasibility. Ghana’s energy Ministry is committing to increase Ghana’s power output by 3x to 10x EVERY YEAR so that the Digital Minister can deliver his AI strategy? Did anyone in Cabinet not protest that this projection in 8 years would mean expanding Ghana’s electricity output by 10,000x? 26. I can bet you any amount that the Energy Minister will deny making any such commitments in Cabinet. Can we have clarity? Can JoyNews check? 27. Page 68 of the strategy defines an "Artificial General Intelligence Lab" as "an AI lab with access to more than 1010 compute". No unit is given at all. In fact, as written it is totally meaningless. What they likely mean is that Ghana will support the establishment of a lab with computing capacity of 10¹⁰ FLOPS (10 gigaFLOPS). 28. The problem is that such a lab would be totally useless. To give you perspective, an iPhone 7 has about 350 gigaFLOPS of capacity. 29. What would be required to meet the Ministry’s 2027 AI target? If for frontier model development, then the following spec would be reasonable: 400,000 16-bit Nvidia B300 GPU units, 1,114 MW of dedicated power (which is 26% of Ghana’s peak demand). And the budget could easily hit US$47.2bn. For less frontier use, we can halve these numbers. 30. Counted in the 64-bit arithmetic that scientific supercomputers are ranked by, Ghana’s 2027 target is 455 times the world’s fastest machine, China’s LineShine at 2.2 exaflops, and 53 times all 500 machines on the list combined. 31. Anyone with the barest exposure to Ghana’s fiscal context can tell the Minister for free that this won’t happen next year. 32. Ghana’s 2035 target of 10²⁵ is 160 times the entire global stock of AI compute today. Even if chips grow 1.4 times more energy-efficient every year, it would draw about 377 GW, 65 times Ghana’s current installed generating capacity. 33. I will be charitable and propose that the strategy’s drafters may have been thinking about training FLOP (note: without the "per second" at the end). For example, GPT-4’s training run used about 2.1×10²⁵ FLOP, the same order of magnitude as Ghana’s 2035 endpoint. 34. Unfortunately, that doesn’t save the strategy. Recast this way, the target collapses the other way. 10²¹ FLOP is about 12 days’ work for one H100 chip at 16-bit precision. 10²⁵ FLOP is one GPT-4-sized training run, which the US$250 million centre could finish in about four months. On that reading the centre meets the 2035 target before its first anniversary. Not meaningful. 35. Given how confusing the overall strategic plan is, would you bank on the first AI compute center and GhanaChat product already being procured at about $270 million? 36. Here are some bare numbers: the budget, per our modelling, maps to about 2,100 GPUs and 4.3 MW of IT load. That alone adds the equivalent of 90% of Ghana’s entire commercial data-centre load in 2024 (4.8 MW). Running it costs about US$76 million a year, which is about six times the revenue of the whole commercial industry. 37. A utilised GPU-hour costs about US$22 at base-case demand, against a market rate of US$6.71 today and roughly US$4.50 averaged over the hardware’s life. The base case thus implies a subsidy of about US$61 million a year. 38. If the concern is about Ministers and their Directors uploading sensitive documents into Gemini or Kimi, then why not a simpler sovereign AI assistant for the civil service first? 39. That would need roughly 144 GPUs: about 7×10¹⁷ operations a second at 8-bit, US$13 million up front and US$6.7 million a year. That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy. Does Ghana really need to train its base model when orchestrators now allow one to host their own data and switch across multiple advanced open-weight models to serve an Assistant or Agentic system? 40. Howzat? — Bright Simons (@BBSimons) October 25, 2026 Mr Simons said if the government’s main concern was protecting sensitive public-sector information from being uploaded to external AI platforms, it could begin by developing a secure AI assistant for civil servants. He estimated that such a system would require about 144 graphics processing units (GPUs), delivering approximately (7 \times 10^{17}) operations per second at eight-bit precision. He put the initial cost at US$13 million, with annual operating expenses of about US$6.7 million. “That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy,” he wrote. Mr Simons also questioned the need to train a foundational AI model from scratch, arguing that systems capable of coordinating multiple existing open-weight models could provide an alternative. He suggested that such an approach could allow government institutions to retain control over their data while drawing on the capabilities of different AI models. The government’s AI strategy includes plans to develop GhanaChat, a national platform intended to compete with international AI services. The proposed system would be trained and hosted in a new AI data centre, with 48 public-sector registries expected to contribute data to improve its understanding of Ghanaian institutions and local needs. The data centre and an accompanying AI Fund are estimated to cost about US$270 million, with additional expenditure expected for registries and related applications. Mr Simons has questioned whether the proposed investment is justified, particularly given the cost of the infrastructure and the resources required to operate it. Mr Simons also challenged the strategy’s computing capacity target for 2027, which he interpreted as (10^{21}) floating-point operations per second (FLOPS). He estimated that meeting the target would require about 200,000 Nvidia chips, 500 megawatts of power and investment of approximately US$24 billion. He said the US$250 million data centre being procured would provide only about one per cent of the stated target. “Clearly, no serious critique of the plan would have okayed such a vision,” he wrote. The estimates are Mr Simons’ assessment of the infrastructure needed to achieve the target. Their assumptions and the precise relationship between the target and the proposed data centre would require independent technical verification. Mr Simons described the apparent shortcomings in the strategy as “classic KATANOMICS”, a term he uses to criticise projects that proceed without sufficient independent scrutiny. He drew a comparison with a sugar factory he says was designed to fail, arguing that inadequate critical review has contributed to the failure of other government programmes. “Throughout the Ministry’s own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged,” he wrote.

items.title: LFR 2026 : le PM Ahmadou A.M Lô appelle les députés à formuler des amendements
items.description: Face au rejet en commission du projet de loi de finances rectificative pour 2026, le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, a appelé les députés à préciser leurs propositions de modification du texte. Il a également défendu les arbitrages budgétaires du gouvernement, qu’il justifie notamment par le coût des subventions énergétiques et les contraintes de financement de l’État. Le débat autour du projet de loi de finances rectificative pour 2026 se poursuit sur fond de désaccord entre le gouvernement et une partie des députés. Prenant la parole sur cette situation, le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, a défendu la démarche de l’exécutif et invité les parlementaires opposés au texte à formuler des propositions concrètes. « Nous demandons aux parlementaires qui ont rejeté en commission la loi de finances rectificative de formuler des amendements », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que les critiques générales ne permettent pas d’identifier les corrections proposées. Le chef du gouvernement a rappelé que l’article 82 de la Constitution encadre le droit d’amendement des députés, notamment en matière de ressources et de charges publiques. Il a ainsi invité les parlementaires à exercer cette prérogative dans le respect des dispositions constitutionnelles. « Le désaccord est légitime dans une démocratie. Cependant, il ne saurait faire perdre de vue la responsabilité commune qui lie les institutions au sein de la nation », a-t-il affirmé. Au-delà du débat institutionnel, le Premier ministre a défendu les ajustements budgétaires proposés par le gouvernement. Il a expliqué que la révision des prévisions pour 2026 résultait notamment de la baisse des recettes attendues, de l’augmentation des charges et des difficultés de mobilisation de certains financements. Le coût du soutien aux prix de l’énergie Les subventions énergétiques occupent une place importante dans l’argumentaire du gouvernement. Selon Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, la hausse des coûts de l’énergie a alourdi les dépenses publiques, obligeant l’État à rechercher des marges de manœuvre dans le budget. Le Premier ministre a soutenu que le gouvernement avait choisi de ne pas répercuter intégralement le choc pétrolier sur les consommateurs. « Nous n’avons pas répercuté intégralement le choc pétrolier sur les Sénégalais. Nous avons absorbé une partie de ce choc en maintenant des prix subventionnés », a-t-il déclaré. Il a expliqué que cette politique de soutien avait entraîné des besoins supplémentaires, alors que les ressources disponibles ne permettaient pas de maintenir l’ensemble des dépenses initialement prévues. Dans ce contexte, le gouvernement a décidé de revoir certains crédits d’investissement. Le projet de LFR prévoit ainsi, selon le Premier ministre, une diminution de 555 milliards de francs CFA des crédits concernés. L’exécutif présente une partie de cette baisse comme un report à 2027 de projets dont les conditions d’exécution n’étaient pas réunies. Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô a également évoqué une baisse de 340 milliards de francs CFA des recettes et une augmentation de 540 milliards des charges et des besoins supplémentaires. Il a insisté sur la nécessité de préserver les dépenses prioritaires, notamment les salaires, la sécurité et la protection sociale. 300 milliards pour les arriérés de paiement Le règlement des arriérés de paiement constitue un autre argument avancé par le gouvernement pour défendre le projet de LFR. Le Premier ministre a indiqué que 300 milliards de francs CFA avaient été inscrits pour commencer à apurer ces engagements, dont le montant global atteindrait 1 956 milliards de francs CFA. Il a mis en avant les conséquences de ces retards pour les entreprises et les travailleurs. Selon lui, le paiement des sommes dues doit permettre à certaines entreprises de retrouver de la trésorerie, de reprendre des chantiers interrompus, de régler leurs fournisseurs et de payer les salaires. Le chef du gouvernement a ainsi appelé les députés à prendre en compte les conséquences économiques et sociales du rejet du texte. Il estime que le débat ne doit pas se limiter aux investissements différés, mais doit également porter sur les moyens de financer les dépenses prioritaires et de régler les engagements de l’État. Enfin, le Premier ministre a insisté sur la nécessité d’un dialogue entre l’exécutif et le Parlement. Il a indiqué avoir proposé au président de l’Assemblée nationale des échanges techniques en amont des prochaines lois de finances, afin de favoriser une meilleure concertation entre les deux institutions. Cette démarche, selon lui, doit permettre de dépasser les divergences et de rechercher des solutions compatibles avec les contraintes budgétaires du pays. C.T.N

items.title: LFR 2026 : Le gouvernement réaffirme le cap de Sénégal 2050
items.description: Face aux contraintes budgétaires, le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô défend une adaptation de la méthode sans renoncer aux ambitions de transformation du pays. Lors de la conférence de presse sur le projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026, tenue le 25 octobre à Dakar, le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô a appelé à dépasser les divergences institutionnelles pour privilégier l’intérêt des Sénégalais. «Le seul objectif qui vaille pour nous tous, c’est d’alléger le fardeau des Sénégalais», a-t-il déclaré, rappelant que la solidité d’une nation se mesure à sa capacité à affronter les difficultés sans perdre de vue ses priorités. Le chef du gouvernement a réaffirmé son attachement à la « Vision Sénégal 2050″, fondée sur la souveraineté économique, la justice sociale, la valorisation des ressources nationales et la création durable de richesses et d’emplois. « Cette ambition n’a pas changé », a-t-il insisté, précisant que seule la méthode évolue. Évoquant les relations avec le Parlement, il a souligné la nécessité de distinguer le débat démocratique de l’entrave à l’action gouvernementale. « Il y a une nuance profonde entre amendements et obstruction du travail gouvernemental », a-t-il affirmé. Le Premier ministre a enfin rappelé les impératifs auxquels l’État doit répondre simultanément. Il s’agit « d’honorer ses engagements, garantir la continuité des services publics et maintenir les investissements essentiels à l’avenir du pays », a-t-il dit. O.BA

items.title: GhanaChat data centre could require $61m annual subsidy – Bright Simons
items.description: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons has questioned the financial viability of Ghana’s proposed US$270 million artificial intelligence (AI) data centre, warning that its operating costs could require substantial annual government subsidies. Referring to an argument he made on Joy News’ Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on Wednesday, Mr Simons said in a post on X, Mr Simons said the facility, which is expected to support the development and hosting of GhanaChat, would have a computing capacity of about 2,100 graphics processing units (GPUs) and an information technology (IT) load of 4.3 megawatts (MW). 1. Readers of this page know by now that JoyNews held a forum on Ghana’s AI strategy and prospects. And the Digital Minister and I got into a serious debate about his Ministry’s plan to build Ghana’s competitor to Gemini, Kimi, ChatGPT, Qwen, Claude, etc. 2. Ghana’s competitor to these global AI platforms is called GhanaChat. 3. It will be trained and hosted in a brand new AI datacenter. 4. 48 registries pooling data from across the public sector will make this AI smarter about Ghana than the foreign ones. 5. The AI datacenter and the "AI Fund" will cost about $270 million. Expect more to be spent on the registries and the apps. A lot of contracts. You can bet that a lot of ICT contractors are very happy. 6. The question is, if we have a couple of hundred million dollars to spend on making AI deliver great benefits for Ghana, should we spend it on GhanaChat, a top-tier AI data center, and the data-pooling system? And should we do it according to the strategy the Ministry has devised? 7. Or could we do much better by more critically assessing all our strategic options and comparing them to the Ministry’s? 8. My argument on the show was that I am not convinced about GhanaChat offering the best value for our money. 9. It would take many pages to explain my position fully. But in this post I will highlight just the most important points. 10. Attached are extracts from page 13, 50, and 68 of Ghana’s AI strategy. 11. If you have even the barest exposure to AI, you can see a massive error. Can you? 12. The target for how much computing capacity the country needs for next year (2027) is indicated as "1021 FLOPS" and the 2035 target as "1025 FLOPS". 13. If this was indeed correct, it would mean that the Ministry would like the entire computing capacity of the country in 2027 to be equivalent to a 1970s desktop computer. Or 2% of the capacity of the 1980 Intel math chip. 14. Howzat? 15. I’m sure you can agree that this would be totally ridiculous if that was the Ministry’s intent. So, what happened? 16. Somebody who didn’t fully understand how FLOPS work must have been involved in the drafting. What was meant to be 10 raised to the power 21 operations per second (10²¹ operations a second) was written out as "1021". Same for "1025". 17. Why wasn’t the error caught? Because in Ghana when doing "consultations", governments rarely engage independent and critical voices who will point out absurdities without fear of offending big men and women. 18. I am not being petty. There is a serious strategic confusion beyond mere typos. 19. Read properly as 10²¹ FLOPS, the Ministry is telling us that by next year it will have some 200,000 of Nvidia’s newest chips in use in Ghana, 500 MW of power devoted to AI, all costing about US$24 billion (close to the Ghanaian government’s entire programmed spending for 2026). 20. The US$250 million AI datacenter now being procured supplies about 1% of this 2027 target. 21. Howzat? 22. Clearly, no serious critique of the plan would have okayed such a vision. Throughout the ministry’s own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged. 23. My first major point here is that this is classic KATANOMICS: the lack of critical policy audiences. This is exactly how a sugar factory that was "designed from the start to fail" was allowed to be built. Many programs and initiatives in Ghana fail for precisely this absence of critical review. 24. In the strategy, you find statements like: "government aggressively building AI compute clusters" and by courting hyperscalers, "to leverage the scaling laws towards building general purpose AI and AGI". Then: "drastically increase Ghana’s energy capacity 0.5 to 1 OOM per year". "OOM" means "order of magnitude". 25. When I challenged the Minister on TV, he confidently rebutted by claiming that the Energy Minister/Ministry has assured him of feasibility. Ghana’s energy Ministry is committing to increase Ghana’s power output by 3x to 10x EVERY YEAR so that the Digital Minister can deliver his AI strategy? Did anyone in Cabinet not protest that this projection in 8 years would mean expanding Ghana’s electricity output by 10,000x? 26. I can bet you any amount that the Energy Minister will deny making any such commitments in Cabinet. Can we have clarity? Can JoyNews check? 27. Page 68 of the strategy defines an "Artificial General Intelligence Lab" as "an AI lab with access to more than 1010 compute". No unit is given at all. In fact, as written it is totally meaningless. What they likely mean is that Ghana will support the establishment of a lab with computing capacity of 10¹⁰ FLOPS (10 gigaFLOPS). 28. The problem is that such a lab would be totally useless. To give you perspective, an iPhone 7 has about 350 gigaFLOPS of capacity. 29. What would be required to meet the Ministry’s 2027 AI target? If for frontier model development, then the following spec would be reasonable: 400,000 16-bit Nvidia B300 GPU units, 1,114 MW of dedicated power (which is 26% of Ghana’s peak demand). And the budget could easily hit US$47.2bn. For less frontier use, we can halve these numbers. 30. Counted in the 64-bit arithmetic that scientific supercomputers are ranked by, Ghana’s 2027 target is 455 times the world’s fastest machine, China’s LineShine at 2.2 exaflops, and 53 times all 500 machines on the list combined. 31. Anyone with the barest exposure to Ghana’s fiscal context can tell the Minister for free that this won’t happen next year. 32. Ghana’s 2035 target of 10²⁵ is 160 times the entire global stock of AI compute today. Even if chips grow 1.4 times more energy-efficient every year, it would draw about 377 GW, 65 times Ghana’s current installed generating capacity. 33. I will be charitable and propose that the strategy’s drafters may have been thinking about training FLOP (note: without the "per second" at the end). For example, GPT-4’s training run used about 2.1×10²⁵ FLOP, the same order of magnitude as Ghana’s 2035 endpoint. 34. Unfortunately, that doesn’t save the strategy. Recast this way, the target collapses the other way. 10²¹ FLOP is about 12 days’ work for one H100 chip at 16-bit precision. 10²⁵ FLOP is one GPT-4-sized training run, which the US$250 million centre could finish in about four months. On that reading the centre meets the 2035 target before its first anniversary. Not meaningful. 35. Given how confusing the overall strategic plan is, would you bank on the first AI compute center and GhanaChat product already being procured at about $270 million? 36. Here are some bare numbers: the budget, per our modelling, maps to about 2,100 GPUs and 4.3 MW of IT load. That alone adds the equivalent of 90% of Ghana’s entire commercial data-centre load in 2024 (4.8 MW). Running it costs about US$76 million a year, which is about six times the revenue of the whole commercial industry. 37. A utilised GPU-hour costs about US$22 at base-case demand, against a market rate of US$6.71 today and roughly US$4.50 averaged over the hardware’s life. The base case thus implies a subsidy of about US$61 million a year. 38. If the concern is about Ministers and their Directors uploading sensitive documents into Gemini or Kimi, then why not a simpler sovereign AI assistant for the civil service first? 39. That would need roughly 144 GPUs: about 7×10¹⁷ operations a second at 8-bit, US$13 million up front and US$6.7 million a year. That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy. Does Ghana really need to train its base model when orchestrators now allow one to host their own data and switch across multiple advanced open-weight models to serve an Assistant or Agentic system? 40. Howzat? — Bright Simons (@BBSimons) October 25, 2026 He said this would add the equivalent of about 90 per cent of Ghana’s entire commercial data centre load in 2024, estimated at 4.8 MW. Mr Simons further estimated the facility’s annual operating costs at approximately US$76 million, about six times the revenue of Ghana’s entire commercial data centre industry. According to Mr Simons, the economics of the proposed facility would be difficult to sustain if it had to sell computing services at prevailing market rates. He estimated that a utilised GPU-hour would cost about US$22 under the project’s base-case demand assumptions, compared with a current market rate of approximately US$6.71 and an estimated average of US$4.50 over the hardware’s operating life. “The base case thus implies a subsidy of about US$61 million a year,” he stated. The estimate raises questions about how the government intends to fund the facility’s recurring expenses and whether revenue from customers using its computing services would be sufficient to cover operating costs. Mr Simons also argued that the proposed data centre would provide only about one per cent of the computing capacity implied by the Ministry’s 2027 target, which he interprets as (10^{21}) floating-point operations per second (FLOPS). He estimated that achieving the target for frontier AI model development would require about 400,000 Nvidia B300 GPU units, dedicated power capacity of 1,114 MW and investment that could reach US$47.2 billion. He said the estimated power requirement would represent about 26 per cent of Ghana’s peak electricity demand. “Anyone with the barest exposure to Ghana’s fiscal context can tell the Minister for free that this won’t happen next year,” he wrote. The figures are Mr Simons’ estimates of what would be required to meet the stated computing target. Their assumptions and the relationship between the target and the government’s planned infrastructure would require independent technical and financial assessment. As an alternative, Mr Simons proposed that Ghana initially develop a sovereign AI assistant for the civil service rather than pursue a large-scale computing facility intended to support a national AI model. He estimated that the system could operate with about 144 GPUs, delivering approximately (7 \times 10^{17}) operations per second at eight-bit precision. He put the initial investment at US$13 million, with annual operating costs of about US$6.7 million. “That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy,” he wrote. Mr Simons also questioned whether Ghana needed to train its own foundational AI model from scratch, suggesting that the government could instead use existing advanced open-weight models while retaining control over its data and how the system is deployed. The proposed data centre forms part of the government’s broader AI strategy, which includes developing GhanaChat as a national platform intended to compete with international services such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude. The plan also includes an AI Fund and the integration of data from 48 public-sector registries to improve the platform’s ability to respond to Ghana-specific needs. The proposed data centre and AI Fund are estimated to cost about US$270 million, with additional expenditure expected for the registries and related applications. Mr Simons’ analysis focuses on whether the proposed investment can be sustained financially and whether a smaller, more targeted system could deliver public-sector benefits at a lower cost. His assessment places the project’s capital expenditure alongside its projected operating costs, potential subsidy requirements and the scale of computing infrastructure implied by the strategy’s longer-term targets.

items.title: Maroc : le soutien aux professionnels du transport routier atteint 2,488 milliards de dirhams en neuf mois
items.description: Un rapport officiel récent met en évidence le coût financier important du soutien exceptionnel direct accordé aux professionnels du transport routier de marchandises et de voyageurs, réactivé au cours de l’année 2026 à la suite de la forte hausse des prix des carburants au Maroc, sur fond de fluctuations des marchés pétroliers internationaux, notamment en raison des tensions au Moyen-Orient. Selon le « Rapport sur la compensation », joint par le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances au projet de loi de finances 2027, le montant total des aides mobilisées au profit des professionnels du transport routier s’est élevé à 2,488 milliards de dirhams sur la période allant de janvier à septembre 2026. Le rapport rappelle que le précédent gouvernement avait réactivé le mécanisme de soutien exceptionnel en faveur des professionnels du transport routier afin de faire face à la forte augmentation des prix du gasoil. Le gouvernement d’Aziz Akhannouch avait versé cette aide par tranches, la dernière ayant été débloquée au début du mois d’octobre. Le montant de l’aide accordée avait alors été revu à la hausse. Sous l’effet des augmentations successives des prix des carburants, le litre de gasoil a dépassé les 16 dirhams dans certaines stations-service. Le rapport revient également sur le contexte international ayant contribué à la hausse des prix des carburants. L’année en cours a été marquée par « un contexte international particulièrement tendu, caractérisé par la persistance des incertitudes géopolitiques, notamment au Moyen-Orient, ainsi que par les perturbations affectant les principales voies d’approvisionnement énergétique », souligne le document. Les tensions autour du détroit d’Ormuz, passage stratégique pour une part importante des hydrocarbures commercialisés dans le monde, ont accentué les risques pesant sur la sécurité des approvisionnements et entraîné une hausse des coûts de transport et d’assurance. « Ces évolutions se sont traduites par de fortes fluctuations sur les marchés de l’énergie et par des pressions croissantes sur les prix internationaux des produits pétroliers » , ajoute le rapport. Dans ce contexte, les cours internationaux des produits énergétiques ont globalement suivi une tendance haussière entre janvier et août 2026. Le prix moyen du pétrole brut Brent a ainsi atteint environ 91 dollars le baril, contre 71 dollars durant la même période de l’année précédente, soit une augmentation de 27,2 %. Le rapport sur la compensation précise que les cours ont évolué dans une large fourchette, comprise entre 60 et 120 dollars le baril, illustrant l’ampleur des fluctuations qui ont marqué le marché pétrolier durant cette période. Pour faire face aux répercussions des fluctuations des prix du pétrole et du gaz, le précédent gouvernement avait pris plusieurs mesures visant à garantir l’approvisionnement du marché national en produits énergétiques. Celles-ci portaient notamment sur l’anticipation des besoins en produits pétroliers, la diversification des sources d’approvisionnement et l’amélioration des conditions d’achat. Parallèlement, des ressources financières supplémentaires ont été mobilisées afin d’atténuer les effets de la hausse des prix internationaux des matières premières, notamment le renchérissement du coût de la subvention du gaz butane et la réactivation du soutien destiné au secteur du transport routier. À ce titre, le budget a été renforcé par l’ouverture de crédits supplémentaires de 8 milliards de dirhams au titre du soutien aux prix. Le montant total des crédits ouverts au titre de la compensation a ainsi été porté à 21,77 milliards de dirhams, selon le rapport. The post Maroc : le soutien aux professionnels du transport routier atteint 2,488 milliards de dirhams en neuf mois appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
