Rather than immediately pursuing a large-scale national model, Mr Simons proposed beginning with a sovereign AI assistant for the civil service. He estimated that such a system could require about 144 graphics processing units (GPUs), delivering approximately (7 \times 10^{17}) operations per second at eight-bit precision. He put the initial cost at US$13 million, with annual operating costs of about US$6.7 million. “That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy,” he wrote. Mr Simons also questioned whether Ghana needed to train its own foundational AI model from scratch, suggesting that systems built around existing open-weight models could allow the government to retain control over its data while using established AI capabilities. His comments raise questions about the scale of investment, technical assumptions and available alternatives that should be assessed as Ghana advances its national AI ambitions.

items.title: Kaduna rally turnout vindicates our mobilisation — City Boy Movement
items.description: — Shoga hails successful APC campaign flag-off, says youth enthusiasm reflects growing support for Tinubu — Says commissioning of Abuja–Kaduna highway section opens economic opportunities for North-West By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA– THE Director-General of the City Boy Movement (CBM), Hon. Francis Oluwatosin Shoga, has commended the large turnout of young Nigerians at Saturday’s flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna. He described the turnout as a testament to the Movement’s sustained grassroots enlightenment and mobilisation efforts in support of President Bola Tinubu. Shoga said the strong turnout of young people at the political gathering reflected their growing interest in the President’s development agenda and their resolve to play an active role in shaping Nigeria’s political and economic future. In a statement titled “Beyond the Road: Unlocking Opportunities, Empowering Young Nigerians, and Building a Prosperous Future,” the CBM Director-General said the enthusiasm at the Kaduna rally was partly driven by sustained grassroots engagements, including the Movement’s mobilisation activities and street walk in Kano. According to him: “The City Boy Movement was proudly on the ground, engaging with young Nigerians and grassroots supporters who came out to demonstrate their commitment to the future of our country. “The enthusiasm witnessed in Kaduna, alongside our grassroots engagement and street walk in Kano, reinforces our conviction that young Nigerians want to be part of a national conversation about development, opportunity, and a more prosperous Nigeria,” he stated. Shoga explained that the Movement’s activities extended beyond mobilising electoral support for Tinubu, stressing that its central mission was to educate and empower young people to understand government policies and take advantage of emerging economic opportunities. He particularly hailed the commissioning of an 81-kilometre section of the Abuja–Kaduna highway during the campaign flag-off, describing the development as a demonstration of the Tinubu administration’s commitment to improving infrastructure and stimulating economic activities in the North-West. According to him, the strategic road corridor linking Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano offers opportunities for agricultural transformation, industrial expansion, regional trade, private investment and employment generation. He noted that improved connectivity could benefit farmers, traders, transport operators and young entrepreneurs by facilitating access to markets, reducing transportation difficulties and encouraging investments in logistics, manufacturing, food processing and related businesses. “The objective is not simply to build infrastructure. It is to create the conditions in which people can build businesses, earn sustainable incomes, create jobs, and improve their standard of living,” Shoga said. He, however, emphasised that infrastructure development must be complemented by sustained security operations, effective intelligence gathering, reliable electricity and investment-friendly policies to unlock the region’s full economic potential. “A good road connects destinations. A secure road connects people to opportunity. Together, infrastructure and security can help unlock the economic potential of an entire region,” he declared. Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, Shoga said the City Boy Movement would intensify its grassroots engagements across the federation, educating young Nigerians about the administration’s reforms while encouraging peaceful democratic participation. He commended the thousands of supporters who participated in the Kaduna rally and Kano mobilisation activities, describing their enthusiasm as an encouragement to the Movement’s nationwide efforts. “Every conversation, every community engagement, and every effort to educate and mobilise people can contribute to a stronger national movement and a more informed citizenry,” he said. Shoga urged young Nigerians to assess the administration’s achievements and challenges, acquire relevant skills, embrace entrepreneurship and make informed political decisions. “Our message is simple: Do not sit on the sidelines while decisions that will shape your future are being made. Get informed, get involved, and make your voice count,” he declared. He reaffirmed the Movement’s commitment to building a generation of informed, enterprising and responsible young Nigerians, stressing that the ultimate success of infrastructure development must be measured by the jobs, businesses and prosperity it creates for ordinary citizens. The post Kaduna rally turnout vindicates our mobilisation — City Boy Movement appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Shadab Khan's maiden ODI century steers Pakistan into tri-series final after thrilling chase against England
items.description: Fortune favours the brave, and on Sunday it favoured Shadab Khan just when he seemed to have been abandoned by it. He had dragged Pakistan from the brink of defeat to within touching distance of victory in the One-day International tri-series match against England. And it had taken extraordinary bravery to do so. With the last wicket standing and Haris Rauf holding firm at the other end, Pakistan needed 27 runs when Shadab swept Gus Atkinson for six over fine leg. Before the sparse crowd at the Gaddafi Stadium could finish celebrating, Atkinson fired a full delivery into Shadab’s pads. England appealed in unison and the umpire raised his finger. Shadab, already regretting the momentary lapse, tapped his bat against his helmet in frustration before reviewing the decision, more out of obligation than hope. Then came the twist. The big screen showed a spike on UltraEdge as the ball passed the bat. The decision was overturned, disbelief gave way to delight and Shadab returned to the crease with a smile. He responded by squeezing Atkinson for four between short third and backward point to bring up his maiden ODI century off 91 balls, then whipped another full delivery through square leg for four. After two dot balls, he pumped Atkinson over long-off for six, leaving Pakistan one hit away from victory. Haris, who had faced 18 balls for his three runs, settled the contest in the next over, drilling debutant Henry Crocombe straight down the ground for four. Pakistan reached 243-9 in 47.1 overs to complete a remarkable one-wicket victory, seal their place in the Oct 31 final and condemn England to another agonising defeat. Shadab remained unbeaten on 113 off 96 balls, with 13 fours and five sixes, while his unbroken 89-run stand with Haris set a record for the highest 10th-wicket partnership in a successful ODI chase, surpassing the previous mark of 64. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, extending his heartiest congratulations to the team, wrote on X: “The last wicket partnership between Shadab and Haris turned the game around. Shadab’s century was spectacular. Well done boys!” He said, “Every run, every wicket and every catch showed the grit, discipline and fighting spirit that define Pakistan.” The unlikely rescue began when Shadab walked in at 103-5 after Arafat Minhas fell for one. Pakistan had been chasing England’s 241 all out but were already in trouble, having lost Fakhar Zaman (10), Saim Ayub (six) and Babar Azam (10) inside seven overs. Saad Baig briefly counter-attacked with 32 off 22 balls, including seven fours, before falling at 74-4. Hasan Nawaz made 15 before Liam Dawson dismissed him at 102, and Arafat followed in the next over. Shadab initially worked his way into the innings, but his task grew harder when Salman Ali Agha, who had made 26 off 49 balls, was caught off Dawson at 121-6. Shaheen Shah Afridi and Razaullah also fell, leaving Pakistan 154-9 after 33.5 overs and still needing 88 runs. Shadab, however, refused to surrender. He reached 32 before Haris arrived, then began to attack with greater conviction. He drove Atkinson over mid-off and pulled him through deep midwicket for boundaries, while a six over midwicket from Razaullah at the other end briefly lifted the pressure before the debutant was bowled by Will Jacks. Shadab’s fifty came off 49 balls, with a six over deep square leg against Crocombe. He then used his feet to Dawson, sweeping a full toss for four and carving another six over wide long-off. Reverse-sweeps and crisp drives through cover kept the chase alive as England struggled to find the final breakthrough. With Haris offering dogged support, Shadab brought up the 50-run stand for the last wicket and then moved into the 90s with a pull for four off Sam Curran. He declined singles at times to retain the strike, taking responsibility for almost every scoring opportunity. His century made him only the third batter to score an ODI hundred at No. 8 or lower. Pakistan’s bowling shines under Shaheen Earlier, Ben Duckett had stood tall with a century as England crumbled around him, managing 241 in 46.4 overs. Shaheen led Pakistan’s attack with 4-46, reducing the visitors to 19-3 inside five overs. Tom Banton fell for four, Joe Root made five and captain Harry Brook was run out for one. Haris then removed Jordan Cox for six as England slumped to 52-4. Duckett rebuilt the innings, reaching his half-century off 56 balls and helping England past 100 in the 20th over. He pulled Haris for four, launched Salman over deep midwicket for six and reverse-hit another boundary. Curran provided the only substantial support, scoring 42 off 52 balls as the pair added 93 for the fifth wicket. Shaheen broke the stand by dismissing Curran, caught at fine leg, before Duckett reached his fifth ODI century off 104 balls — his first against Pakistan. He made 105 off 111 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes, before Arafat had him caught at short fine leg for 187-7. Razaullah took two wickets, including Will Jacks for 13, while Arafat also dismissed Jamie Overton for 10. Atkinson’s unbeaten 36 off 28 balls, featuring three sixes, lifted England to 241 before Shaheen dismissed Crocombe for eight to finish with four wickets. England’s total looked competitive when Pakistan collapsed, but Shadab’s extraordinary innings turned the match on its head and carried the hosts into the final. Haris Rauf compounded England’s troubles when Jordan Cox edged behind to Babar Azam for six, leaving the visitors struggling at 52-4 in the 10th over. Duckett, however, refused to let the innings unravel completely. The left-hander brought up his half-century off 56 balls as England reached 100 in the 20th over, keeping the scoreboard moving with well-timed cuts, drives and sweeps. He pulled Haris through midwicket for four before launching Salman Ali Agha over deep midwicket for six. Duckett also produced a reverse-hit boundary against Salman and pierced the covers with a crisp drive off Shadab Khan. At the other end, Sam Curran provided the only meaningful support, counter-attacking with a series of boundaries. He charged down the track to lift Saim over mid-on and later rocked back to dispatch the spinner through midwicket. The pair added 93 runs for the fifth wicket, taking England from 52-4 to 145 before Shaheen returned to break the stand in the 27th over. Curran, who scored 42 off 52 balls with five fours, top-edged a pull off a short delivery to Salman at fine leg. Duckett continued to hold the innings together, reaching his fifth ODI century off 104 balls and his first against Pakistan. He struck 105 off 111 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes, before Arafat dismissed him in the 37th over, with Salman taking the catch at short fine leg. England then lost Will Jacks (13) to Razaullah, who took a sharp return catch for his maiden ODI wicket, while Liam Dawson (five) fell to another short ball, caught by Shadab at deep square leg. Arafat also removed Jamie Overton (10), caught by Babar at long-off. Gus Atkinson offered late resistance with an unbeaten 36 off 28 balls, including three sixes, helping England cross 200. Shaheen eventually ended the innings by dismissing debutant Henry Crocombe for eight, with Babar completing the catch.

items.title: LFR 2026 : le gouvernement justifie le report de 555 milliards de francs CFA d’investissements
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, a défendu les arbitrages opérés dans le projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR) pour 2026, ce dimanche 25 novembre, en mettant en avant la baisse des recettes, la hausse des dépenses énergétiques et les difficultés de mobilisation des financements extérieurs. Selon lui, les ajustements budgétaires visent à préserver les dépenses prioritaires et à reporter certains investissements dont l’exécution n’était pas assurée avant la fin de l’année. Le gouvernement assume ses choix budgétaires. Lors de sa prise de parole consacrée à la situation née de l’examen du projet de loi de finances rectificative pour 2026, le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, a défendu les mesures d’ajustement proposées par l’exécutif. Il a notamment expliqué que la révision des prévisions budgétaires répondait à des contraintes liées à la mobilisation des recettes et à l’augmentation de certaines dépenses. « La loi de finances rectificative est une nécessité objective. Les équilibres ont été modifiés ; il faut donc les changer », a-t-il déclaré, en présentant les principaux facteurs ayant conduit le gouvernement à revoir ses prévisions. Selon le chef du gouvernement, l’État fait face à trois contraintes majeures. Il a évoqué une baisse des recettes de 340 milliards de francs CFA, une augmentation de 540 milliards des charges et des besoins supplémentaires, principalement liés aux subventions énergétiques et au renforcement des moyens des forces de défense et de sécurité. À ces difficultés s’ajoute la nécessité de contenir un déficit déjà élevé dans un contexte de fortes contraintes sur les finances publiques. Face à cette situation, le gouvernement affirme avoir privilégié la préservation des dépenses essentielles, notamment les salaires, les missions fondamentales de l’État, la sécurité et la protection sociale. Les arbitrages ont ainsi porté sur des investissements dont les conditions d’exécution n’étaient pas réunies. Le projet de LFR prévoit, selon le Premier ministre, une baisse de 555 milliards de francs CFA des crédits d’investissement. Le chef du gouvernement soutient toutefois qu’une partie de ces crédits correspond à des projets reportés plutôt qu’abandonnés. « Je veux être clair : il s’agit, pour une partie, d’investissements différés à l’année prochaine », a-t-il expliqué, estimant que le maintien de crédits destinés à des projets qui ne peuvent pas être exécutés dans les délais ne constitue pas nécessairement la meilleure utilisation des ressources publiques. « Une inscription budgétaire, oui, pour un hôpital, pour l’eau, pour un forage, mais si ça ne peut pas s’exécuter, reportons ce crédit à l’année prochaine pour pouvoir exécuter d’autres dépenses », a-t-il indiqué. Les recettes du PRES en question Les arbitrages concernent notamment les dépenses prévues dans le cadre du Plan de redressement économique et social (PRES). D’après Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, les ressources encaissées au titre de ce programme s’élevaient à 173 milliards de francs CFA à la fin du mois de septembre. Cette mobilisation, inférieure aux prévisions, a conduit le gouvernement à différer 295 milliards de francs CFA de dépenses. Le Premier ministre a souligné que certains investissements avaient été programmés en fonction des recettes attendues du PRES. Il estime que les difficultés de mobilisation de ces ressources doivent être prises en compte dans l’appréciation des choix budgétaires. Les financements extérieurs constituent un autre facteur de contrainte. Le chef du gouvernement a fait état de 239 milliards de francs CFA de financements attendus mais non mobilisés. Cette situation a nécessité, selon lui, des arbitrages sur les projets pouvant être poursuivis en 2026 et ceux dont l’exécution doit être reportée à 2027. Il a néanmoins assuré que les engagements bénéficiant de financements sécurisés avaient été préservés. Plus de 110 milliards de francs CFA auraient ainsi pu être financés à partir du PRES, notamment pour des projets universitaires, des infrastructures de santé et l’aéroport de Ziguinchor. Le gouvernement prévoit également de poursuivre en 2027 plusieurs projets hospitaliers, notamment à Mbour, Kaolack, Ziguinchor, Saint-Louis et Matam. Les travaux d’assainissement de Touba, les centres de santé, les agropoles ainsi que certaines infrastructures scolaires et sanitaires figurent également parmi les projets évoqués par le Premier ministre. Au-delà des investissements, la LFR doit permettre de dégager des marges de manœuvre pour régler une partie des arriérés de paiement de l’État. Le gouvernement a inscrit 300 milliards de francs CFA à cette fin, alors que leur montant global est estimé à 1 956 milliards de francs CFA par le chef du gouvernement. Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô a insisté sur les conséquences économiques de ces retards de paiement, notamment pour les entreprises du bâtiment et des travaux publics, leurs fournisseurs et les travailleurs mobilisés sur les chantiers. Pour le Premier ministre, les ajustements proposés doivent permettre de concilier la continuité des services publics, le règlement d’une partie des engagements de l’État et la poursuite des investissements prioritaires, dans un contexte de ressources limitées. Cheikh Tidiane NDIAYE

items.title: My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Actress Uzoamaka Power, known for her role in The Call of My Life, has revealed that her father’s perception of acting initially made her afraid to pursue her dream of becoming an actress. Speaking during an interview on the Tea With Tay podcast, Power recalled how her father frequently criticised actresses whenever they appeared on television, questioning their dressing and commitment to education. “With my father, I was cowardly about pursuing my dreams because my father’s idea of acting, the way he saw acting, was prostitution,” she said. According to her, watching films with her father often meant listening to his disapproval of the women appearing on screen. “Anytime we watched a film, he was always criticising the women. He would be like, ‘Don’t they have parents? Look at what they are wearing, and they are in the university. When do they have time to study?’” Despite his reservations, Power said she had always been certain about her desire to become an actress and believed she would succeed in the profession. “I had a knowing in me that I was going to be an actor, and I knew I was going to succeed doing this thing I love doing,” she said. The actress, however, acknowledged that her father’s concerns came from a place of care, explaining that he wanted her to pursue a career he considered more financially secure. “I understood that he was looking out for me and he wanted the best for me. He also knew these kinds of jobs were not sustainable. You needed, like, an office job,” she recalled. Speaking further about her personality and how she handles perceptions of arrogance, Power maintained that she had never felt the need to diminish herself to make others comfortable. “I have never felt the need to downplay myself or to make myself feel small for the benefit of everyone else. I have always known who I am. I have always known my shortcomings, to be honest,” she said. She added that being aware of her strengths and limitations had helped her remain comfortable with herself, regardless of how others interpreted her confidence. “I am very honest with myself about where I am, what I am doing, what I am capable of, what I am unable to do, and whether I am willing to learn. “So, I have just been myself, really. And if anyone considers that not being humble, I am sorry, I can’t,” she said. The post My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Labé : Fatoumata Binta Cherif Diallo couronnée Miss Moyenne Guinée 2026
items.description: À l'issue d'une soirée riche en élégance et en émotion ce samedi 24 octobre à Labé, l'étudiante en sociologie Fatoumata Binta Cherif Diallo a décroché l'écharpe régionale de Miss Guinée 2026-2027. Elle portera haut les couleurs du Fouta Djallon lors de la grande finale nationale à Conakry a constaté sur place la rédaction de votre quotidien électronique Guinéenews . L ’espace culturel « Ka Werdè » de Labé a vibré au rythme de la beauté, de l’intelligence et de l’élégance foutaniennes hier soir . Cet écrin culturel a accueilli la très attendue cérémonie de présélection du prestigieux concours Miss Guinée 2026-2027 pour la région de la Moyenne Guinée. Au terme d’une compétition relevée, c’est Mademoiselle Fatoumata Binta Cherif Diallo, étudiante en troisième année de sociologie à l’Université de Labé, qui a su charmer le jury et le public. Elle s’est imposée face à ses concurrentes et succède ainsi pour porter la lourde et noble responsabilité de représenter sa région natale sur la scène nationale. Visiblement émue mais résolue, la nouvelle ambassadrice de la beauté foutanienne n’a pas caché sa gratitude. « Je suis très contente que le comité d’organisation ait placé sa confiance en moi en me confiant la couronne de Miss Moyenne Guinée 2026-2027. Je suis consciente de la responsabilité qui m’incombe et je suis déterminée à aller jusqu’au bout », a-t-elle déclaré à chaud. Consciente que l'étape de Labé n'est qu'un prélude, la jeune lauréate aborde la suite avec lucidité et rigueur . « Pour remporter le concours national, je ne dirais pas grand-chose, car après tout, Dieu a le dernier mot. Ce que je peux vous assurer, c’est que je représenterai dignement la région de la Moyenne Guinée, et je le ferai de tout mon cœur. Je sais que l’aventure ne fait que commencer, et je compte me préparer très sérieusement pour pouvoir assumer mes responsabilités. » Interrogée sur la recette de son succès, celle qui avoue dompter difficilement son stress d’ordinaire livre un message inspirant à la jeunesse et aux futures candidates. Pour elle, la clé réside dans l'intime conviction de sa propre valeur :« Tout d’abord, j’ai pris beaucoup de plaisir à participer à cette présélection. D’habitude, je suis stressée, mais il faut savoir une chose : ayez confiance en vous, en vos rêves et surtout en vos qualités. C’est extrêmement important. Lorsque j’étais sur le podium, je me disais : « Non, il n’y a pas d’autre choix, je dois assumer » », confie-t-elle avec assurance. Cette soirée mémorable s'est également clôturée par la distinction de deux autres brillants talents féminins qui accompagneront la dynamique de cette édition régionale. Anne Marie Camara et Finda Jeannette Tinguino ont été respectivement couronnées première et deuxième dauphines. Le compte à rebours est désormais lancé pour Fatoumata Binta Cherif Diallo et son staff. items.title: LFR 2026 : Le Premier ministre explique les arbitrages budgétaires
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô a défendu, dimanche 25 octobre 2026, les ajustements budgétaires proposés par le gouvernement sur le projet de loi de finances rectificative (LFR). Il invoque une baisse de 340 milliards de FCFA des recettes et une hausse de 540 milliards des charge s. Le gouvernement entend faire de l’allègement du coût de la vie la priorité du débat sur la loi de finances rectificative. « Le seul objectif qui doit nous guider tous, c’est d’alléger le fardeau des Sénégalais », a déclaré le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô, lors de la conférence de presse tenue dimanche 25 octobre. Le chef du gouvernement a distingué la différence entre amendements parlementaires et obstruction à l’action du gouvernement. « Il y a une nuance profonde entre l’obstruction au travail du gouvernement et les amendements de l’Assemblée nationale », a-t-il souligné, invitant les députés à formuler des propositions concrètes. « Nous demandons au Parlement de se déterminer clairement . J’espère qu’il sera dit aux Sénégalais ce qu’ils veulent, sans rester dans des généralités. » Le Premier ministre a également rappelé la responsabilité juridique des parlementaires dans cet exercice. «Formuler un amendement vous met face à la responsabilité de la constitutionnalité », a-t-il rappelé. Trois contraintes budgétaires majeures Le chef du gouvernement a identifié trois contraintes principales. La première est une baisse prévisionnelle des recettes de 340 milliards de FCFA. La deuxième correspond à une hausse des charges de 540 milliards de FCFA, liée notamment aux besoins supplémentaires du secteur énergétique et au renforcement des moyens des forces de défense et de sécurité. La troisième tient à la nécessité de contenir un déficit déjà élevé, dans un contexte de fortes tensions sur les finances publiques. Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lô a par ailleurs rappelé que les budgets de 2024, 2025 et 2026 avaient été élaborés dans un contexte difficile. «En 2024, 2025 et 2026, le budget a été élaboré sous contraintes. Pourquoi nous le reprocher aujourd’hui », s’est-il interrogé. Il a par ailleurs souligné que la loi de finances initiale avait été approuvée sous le précédent gouvernement, présentant la LFR comme un instrument d’ajustement des recettes et des dépenses, en fonction des évolutions. O.BA

items.title: Cyclisme : Awa Bamogo et Soumaïla Ilboudo s’imposent au Grand Prix FASP Wassa Bondo
items.description: Le Grand Prix cycliste du Fonds d'Appui au Sport et à la Presse Privée Wassa Bondo a rendu son verdict ce 25 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. En hommes, Soumaïla Ilboudo a devancé son coéquipier de l'AS Bessel, Souleymane Koné, de quelques millisecondes au sprint final. En dames, Awa Bamogo a écrasé la concurrence au point de boucler un tour d'avance. Une 5e édition qui tombe à pic, à cinq jours du lancement de la 37e édition du Tour cycliste international du Faso. La course hommes a été disputée sur 122,3 kilomètres, bouclés en 146 minutes et 0,3 seconde à une vitesse moyenne de 44,191 km/h, soit un kilomètre de plus à l'heure que lors de la veille selon la ministre présente. Au terme d'un sprint final serré, Soumaïla Ilboudo a franchi la ligne en premier devant Souleymane Koné, tous deux membres de l'AS Bessel. Mohamadi Ilboudo et Paul Domont ont complété le podium. Le vainqueur repart avec 2 millions de francs CFA et son trophée. Le deuxième a reçu 1 million de francs CFA et le troisième 500 000 francs CFA. Des délégations malienne et nigérienne ont également pris part à la compétition. En dames, Awa Bamogo n'a laissé aucun suspense. Sur les huit tours de l'Avenue Capitaine Thomas Sankara, elle a distancé ses concurrentes au point de terminer avec un tour d'avance sur les autres, en compagnie de la deuxième, Lamoussa Zoungrana. Sawadogo Latifa a pris la troisième place. Awa Bamogo repart avec 1 million de francs CFA et un trophée, Lamoussa Zoungrana avec 750 000 francs CFA et la troisième avec 500 000 francs CFA. Un tremplin assumé vers le Tour du Faso-©Faso7 Annick Pikbougoum/Zingué Ouattara, ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l'Emploi, présente sur le circuit, a salué la performance et y a lu un signal positif pour l'échéance qui approche. « D'ici quelques jours, nous allons commencer le Tour du Faso et ça voudrait dire que notre équipe nationale aussi est prête. Le soutien du gouvernement est total au niveau de tous les sports, et en particulier pour le cyclisme » , a-t-elle déclaré. Ida Ouédraogo/Paré, directrice générale du FASP Wassa Bondo, a précisé que cette édition, habituellement tenue à Bobo-Dioulasso et prévue cette année à Gaoua, a finalement été délocalisée à Ouagadougou pour préserver les conditions physiques des athlètes avant le Tour du Faso. « Nous avons tenu à accompagner le processus de préparation des équipes pour cette grande échéance. Aujourd'hui, le cyclisme a démontré, s'il en était encore besoin, sa capacité de mobilisation, de rassemblement et de fraternité » , a-t-elle indiqué. Soumaïla Ilboudo, victorieux du jour, ne cache pas sa confiance à l'approche du Tour du Faso. La moyenne de 44,191 km/h enregistrée ce 25 octobre lui semble de bon augure . « Je pense que si Dieu le veut, ça ira » , a-t-il simplement déclaré, avec le calme de ceux qui ont laissé parler les jambes avant la bouche. La 37e édition du Tour cycliste international du Faso, qui se tiendra du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, marque le retour de la compétition sur le calendrier de l'Union Cycliste Internationale après deux années d'absence. Le prochain tour du Faso, c'est dix étapes, douze équipes, dont les Étalons cyclistes du Burkina Faso et plusieurs formations africaines et européennes. Le Grand Prix Wassa Bondo de ce dimanche aura servi, pour les coureurs burkinabè, de répétition générale grandeur nature. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Cyclisme : Awa Bamogo et Soumaïla Ilboudo s'imposent au Grand Prix FASP Wassa Bondo est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: GPL 2026/27: Asante Kotoko fight back to hold AshantiGold in derby
items.description: Asante Kotoko came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw against FC AshantiGold 04 at the Len Clay Stadium in Obuasi in the Ghana Premier League. Kotoko travelled to Obuasi seeking consecutive league victories after beating Young Apostles 2-1, but had to settle for a point against an AshantiGold side that had won all three of their home matches since gaining promotion to the top flight. The hosts took the lead shortly before half-time when Samuel Fosu Boateng’s long-range strike took a slight deflection off Joseph Amoah before finding the back of the net. Kotoko goalkeeper Aziz Dari Haruna had earlier kept his side in the contest with a fine save, ensuring the visitors went into the break trailing by just one goal. AshantiGold resumed the second half looking to protect their advantage, but Kotoko found a way back into the game through Asiedu. The midfielder produced a powerful free-kick in the 63rd minute to beat the AshantiGold goalkeeper and bring the visitors level, giving the Porcupine Warriors renewed hope of completing a comeback. Both sides subsequently searched for a winner, with AshantiGold threatening to regain the lead. However, Haruna came to Kotoko’s rescue again in the 79th minute with another important save to deny the hosts. Neither team could find a decisive goal in the closing stages, leaving the contest level at 1-1. The result extends Kotoko’s winless run away from home in the league to four matches, having entered the encounter without a victory in their previous three away fixtures. For AshantiGold, the draw ends their run of three consecutive home victories since returning to the top flight. The two sides went into the match separated by just one point, with Kotoko on 12 points in eighth place and AshantiGold on 11 points in 10th position. Kotoko will now turn their attention to a meeting with league leaders Medeama, while AshantiGold prepare to face Swedru All Blacks in their next league fixture.

items.title: Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026?
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi It appears music powerhouse Ayodeji Balogun is keeping his fans hanging too long on a thread after he made a promise of his seventh solo studio album “coming soon” in June 2026. Three months down the line, the wait continues without any actual date in sight. The Wizkid FC, his fanatical fans, wouldn’t throw any tantrum about this, but the question has to be asked as to what is keeping the “Holla at Ya Boy” star from unleashing his “Sexy” (title of his seventh studio album) on the music scene. The fact that the superstar started 2026 on the up and up hasn’t helped matters because it felt pretty much like he gave his fans a shot in the arm and left them high and dry. He began the year with ‘Jogodo’, a collaboration with Asake that set the stage for their joint extended play, ‘REAL, Vol. 1’. He subsequently expanded his catalogue with releases involving Latin music, British R&B and other contemporary sounds, reinforcing his reputation as an artiste comfortable working across musical boundaries. One of the defining moments of his 2026 output was the January release of ‘REAL, Vol. 1’, a four-track EP with Asake. Released on January 23, the project brought together two generations of Nigerian music stars whose styles have helped shape the contemporary Afrobeats sound. The project followed the success of their earlier collaborations, including ‘MMS’ on Asake’s 2024 album, ‘Lungu Boy’. It featured songs such as ‘Jogodo’, ‘Iskolodo’ and ‘Turbulence’, combining infectious rhythms, melodic hooks and elements of contemporary African dance music. ‘Jogodo’, released ahead of the EP in January, served as the lead single and generated anticipation for the full project. The collaboration offered fans an opportunity to hear the two singers build on their established musical chemistry. The singer continued this international run with ‘Alive’, a collaboration with British singer-songwriter Jorja Smith, released on July 2. The song blended R&B and Afrobeats, with production by P2J, and appeared ahead of Smith’s third studio album, ‘What Are The Odds’. Another notable release was ‘Coca Body’, featuring Dutch rapper and singer Frenna, British-Nigerian singer Odeal and Wizkid. Released in July, the song brought together the artistes’ melodic approaches in a record that drew on Afrobeats, R&B and hip-hop influences. These collaborations highlighted Wizkid’s continued willingness to explore different sounds while maintaining the relaxed vocal delivery that has become a hallmark of his music. Beyond his recorded collaborative outputs, his fans still await his next solo effort. In June, he unveiled ‘Sexy’ as the title of his seventh studio album at a listening party in Paris. However, a release date and full tracklist had not been announced at the time of the report. The post Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026? appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GPL 2026/27: Bechem United hammer Debibi United
items.description: Bechem United were dominant in their Ghana Premier League matchday eight fixtures, making light work of newly-promoted Debibi United. The Bechem-based side recorded an emphatic 3-0 win over Debibi to bounce back to winning ways after defeat in their last league outing. The home side opened the scoring in Bechem in the 36th minute of the encounter when Isaiah Nyarko broke the deadlock to give them a deserved lead. Debibi United went into the break trailing by one goal with hopes of overturning the fixture. However, they found themselves two goals behind Bechem after 71 minutes. Kelvin Appiah scored to double the lead for Bechem and stretch their lead over the newcomers. Nine minutes after scoring his first goal of the game, Appiah was on the scoresheet again to complete his brace and hand Bechem United all three points with a 3-0 final score at home. The result sees Bechem United clinb into the top half of the table after eight games, amassing 13 points in that run. Debibi, on the other hand, now have just one win from their last five games, and sit 16th on the league table.

items.title: 2026/27 Ghana League: Port City snatch late winner to deepen Karela United woes
items.description: Port City scored twice in the closing stages to secure a 2-1 victory over Karela United in their Ghana Premier League Matchweek Eight encounter on Sunday in Tamale. Owusu Ansah scored the decisive goal in the 89th minute to hand the newly promoted side all three points after Iddi Mahfuz had briefly restored parity for the hosts. The visitors broke the deadlock in the 77th minute when Owusu Ansah found the net to give Port City the advantage. Karela responded nine minutes later, with Mahfuz scoring in the 86th minute to make it 1-1 and raise hopes of salvaging a point at home. However, Port City struck again just three minutes later, as Owusu Ansah completed his brace to restore their lead and secure a crucial victory. The result ends Karela United’s unbeaten home run this season and extends their losing streak to two matches. The defeat leaves Karela 14th in the league standings with nine points from eight matches, having recorded three wins and five defeats without a draw. Port City, meanwhile, return to winning ways after a draw and a defeat in their previous two matches. The victory lifts the newly promoted side to fourth place with 14 points from eight games. They have now recorded four wins, two draws and two defeats. Port City will hope to build on the important away victory as they seek to maintain their strong start to life in the top flight, while Karela will be eager to halt their slide in the coming fixtures.

items.title: Agou/accès à l’eau potable : La population de Nyamessi informée d’un projet d’installation d’un forage dans leur localité
items.description: Agou-Gadzepé, 25 oct. (ATOP) – La population du village de Nyamessi dans la commune Agou 2, a été informée, le samedi 24 octobre, lors d’une rencontre d’échanges avec le député Yossah Yawotsè, d’un projet d’installation d’un forage dans leur localité. Ce projet est une initiative de l’Association perle du monde (PMA) avec pour ambition de combler le besoin en eau potable de la population. En dehors de la présentation du projet hydraulique, la rencontre a aussi servi de cadre d’échanges sur les projets en cours dans le village notamment ceux liés à l’agriculture et au déploiement de l’électricité. Les doléances relatives aux infrastructures routières, sanitaires et écolières ont été également rappelées par la population. L’honorable Yossah a indiqué que ce projet hydraulique en cours est une réponse à un des besoins exprimés par la population lors de sa dernière visite. Il a réitéré son engagement à poursuivre des plaidoyers auprès des partenaires et autorités compétentes pour que des réponses soient trouvées à d’autres problèmes de développement du milieu. Il a rappelé aux jeunes la nécessité de participer aux activités communautaires, de s’instruire ou d’apprendre un métier pour assurer un avenir meilleur. Aussi a-t-il invité la population à cultiver l’amour du prochain, la cohésion sociale et le vivre ensemble pour une paix durable. La présidente de l’association PMA, Gontier Betty a exprimé sa reconnaissance à la population pour son accueil chaleureux. Elle a salué le dynamisme notamment des femmes de la localité puis promis revenir avec d’autres initiatives pour accompagner ces dernières dans leurs différentes activités génératrices de revenus. Mme Gontier a invité les villageois à d’ores et déjà réfléchir sur la mise en place d’un comité de gestion de cet ouvrage. La cérémonie s’est terminée par la visite d’exploration du terrain par les techniciens de l’association PMA pour la détection de l’endroit idéal où sera installé l’ouvrage. ATOP/BSM/MET/HKM

items.title: FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions
items.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has disbursed the sum of ₦38.93 billion to 166 public tertiary institutions, nationwide, under the Needs Assessment Revitalisation Fund. Details of the disbursement contained in a statement by the Head, Media Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, Efe Ovuakporie in Abuja, yesterday, showed that beneficiaries included 79 universities, 46 polytechnics and 41 colleges of education. The funds would support approved projects aimed at addressing infrastructure gaps and improving teaching and learning facilities across the institutions. The university component accounts for ₦28.5 billion for 79 institutions, while 46 polytechnics have allocations totalling ₦5.8 billion. The 41 colleges of education received ₦4.7 billion. The statement read in part, “The intervention forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to address the needs of public universities and support the implementation of agreed measures under the Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Government and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU). “The funds are expected to enable beneficiary institutions to commence or advance approved projects addressing critical infrastructure and other identified institutional needs, with the overall objective of strengthening the quality of tertiary education in Nigeria. The disbursement underscores the importance of effective coordination between the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Education and beneficiary institutions in ensuring that approved public funding translates into tangible improvements in educational infrastructure and institutional capacity.” The post FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kozah / lutte contre le cancer du sein et du col de l’utérus : Les lycéennes de Lama Kpedah sensibilisées au dépistage précoce
items.description: Kara, 25 oct. (ATOP) – Plus de 250 élèves filles du lycée de Lama Kpédah ont été sensibilisées au dépistage précoce du cancer du sein et du col de l’utérus le 22 octobre dans l’enceinte dudit établissement. L’activité de sensibilisation organisée par l’association FemSansCancer (F.S.C.) avec l’appui de la Fondation TOMFEI, intervient dans le cadre de la campagne annuelle de communication « d’Octobre Rose », visant à éveiller la conscience des jeunes filles sur ce mal silencieux. L’objectif principal est de contribuer à la lutte contre le cancer du sein et du col de l’utérus au Togo à travers la sensibilisation au dépistage précoce et à collecter des fonds pour la recherche. Spécifiquement il s’est agi d’apprendre la bonne pratique de l’auto-examen des seins, de connaître les signes et symptômes du cancer du sein à partir du poster de citrons. Il est aussi question d’améliorer les connaissances des groupes cibles sur les cancers du col de l’utérus et du sein, de les inciter au dépistage régulier par frottis cervico-utérin ou test HPV, ainsi que de briser les tabous et idées préconçues. Elles ont exécuté des exercices pratiques pour mieux s’adapter aux différentes techniques d’auto consultation et aux premiers gestes à adopter en cas de présence des symptômes. Comprendre le cancer du sein pour mieux agir Mme Zenabou au micro Le président de la Fédération togolaise des organisations de lutte contre les maladies non transmissibles au Togo (FETO-LMNT), Dr. Kouvahey Damien, a défini le cancer du sein, comme étant « le développement anormal des cellules au niveau du sein dû aux causes multiples dont les hormones et l’âge ». Selon lui, plus on avance en âge, plus le risque augmente, précisant qu’aujourd’hui le cancer est aussi là parce que les gens mangent très mal, trop sucré, trop salé, trop gras, avec beaucoup de toxiques. « Nous ne faisons pas assez d’activités physiques, nous buvons beaucoup d’alcool et consommons trop de tabac. Si nos anticorps ne sont pas aptes à tuer ces cellules anormales, le cancer s’installe », a-t-il renchéri. Il a dit que le cancer du sein apparait sous les signes d’un nodule avec saignement, une peau d’orange, ou un sein qui grossit plus que l’autre et change de forme. Dr. Kouvahey a exhorté les jeunes filles à l’autopalpation pour mieux découvrir leurs seins devant le miroir avec les yeux et les mains. Dès qu’il y a un petit signe, il a-t-il expliqué, il faut courir en parler à sa maman ou aller à l’hôpital. Le spécialiste a enfin insisté sur les gestes qui sauvent notamment, dormir suffisamment, faire de l’activité physique et surtout, ne jamais utiliser de pommades pour faire grossir les seins. Que retenir du cancer du col de l’utérus Pour le col de l’utérus, il a éclairé son auditoire que c’est « un virus, appelé le papillomavirus humain (HPV) qui peut rester au niveau du col pendant 10 à 15 ans et se multiplie pour donner des lésions aboutissant au cancer ». Il a convié les jeunes filles à éviter les rapports sexuels précoces, de partenaires multiples, à introduire certains produits chimiques dans l’anus pour faire grossir les fesses ou dans le vagin pour plus de plaisir, car ces pratiques dangereuses favorisent le cancer du col. Il faut aussi pratiquer la bonne hygiène et surtout à aller se faire dépister régulièrement par frottis ou test HPV. Mme Zénabou Moumouni, présidente de l’association FemSansCancer et survivante du cancer du sein, a fait savoir que leur démarche consiste à parler des cancers féminins aux jeunes filles du lycée de Lama-Kpédah, pour qu’elles s’approprient les bonnes pratiques de l’auto-examen et l’observation de ses seins. Elle a exhorté les jeunes filles à pratiquer l’exercice physique, avoir une alimentation saine et équilibrée, à éviter de fumer. « La chicha, que les jeunes prennent beaucoup, est 10 fois plus dangereuse que la cigarette », a indiqué Mme Zénabou. Seule la vaccination chez les adolescentes et le frottis cervico-vaginal ou le test HPV chez adulte, peuvent réduire le cancer, a-t-elle souligné. Tébié Leticia et Kanema Vanessa, se sont réjouies de cette initiative qui vient à point nommé les éclairer sur beaucoup de choses qu’elles ignoraient. « ces connaissances nouvelles nous érigent désormais en ambassadrices de lutte contre ces cancers auprès de nos camarades, mamans et nos sœurs », a confié Leticia. Portée sur les fonts baptismaux en 20217, l’association FemSansCancer informe les jeunes filles et femmes à travers les sensibilisations et les formations, tout en réconfortant et soutenant les victimes qui traversent cette épreuve afin qu’elles évitent l’isolement. FemSansCancer compte à ce jour plus de onze mille femmes sensibilisées et formées sur l’étendue du territoire national. ATOP/AK/SG/HKM

items.title: Igbo must unite, build alliances to produce president — Soludo
items.description: …Opens up on inclusion in APC presidential campaign council …Says Igbo identity no reason to back Obi … Declares victory over Monday sit-at-home, says Anambra back to life By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has said the Igbo must unite and build strategic alliances across Nigeria to stand a chance of producing the country’s president. Soludo said the South-East must overcome political divisions and forge strategic alliances with other regions to strengthen its bargaining power. He cited the alliance-building approach associated with First Republic political leader, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, arguing that the Igbo needed a broader national support base to realise their presidential ambition. He also pointed to President Bola Tinubu’s political alliances as an example of the importance of coalition-building in securing power. Gov. Soludo who spoke exclusively with Vanguard, declared that he and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) would support President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, explaining why he accepted an appointment in the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council despite belonging to another party. The Governor said APGA’s leadership had collectively adopted Tinubu for a second term and resolved not to field a presidential candidate, adding that the decision was consistent with the party’s tradition of supporting presidents irrespective of their political platforms. He recalled that former Anambra governors Peter Obi and Willie Obiano had similarly supported presidential candidates from other parties. Speaking through his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Christian Aburime, Gov. Soludo said he had since, communicated APGA’s position to President Tinubu during the President’s visit to Anambra to inaugurate landmark projects, including the Government House, Solution Fun City and roads. Obi’s Igbo identity no reason to back him On expectations that Soludo should support his predecessor and the presidential flag bearer of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, Aburime said the two politicians belonged to different parties and did not share the same political ideology. He acknowledged that Obi was qualified to contest the presidency but maintained that shared ethnicity should not determine political support. “Politics shouldn’t be based on emotion or sentiment. They have different ideologies,” he said, insisting that Nigerians should support parties based on their capacity to improve citizens’ lives rather than ethnic or regional considerations. Aburime also dismissed the assumption that Anambra voters would repeat their overwhelming support for Obi in 2023, declaring that the political dynamics had changed. “2023 is gone. 2027 is not going to be 2023,” he said, expressing confidence that APGA members would vote for Tinubu. Defends Tinubu’s economic reforms On the removal of fuel subsidy and foreign exchange reforms, Aburime said Soludo supported Tinubu’s economic policies, describing them as painful but necessary measures to address longstanding structural weaknesses. He argued that the previous practice of printing money to sustain the economy was unsustainable, adding that the reforms would eventually yield benefits. On whether Tinubu had influenced former President Muhammadu Buhari to adopt better economic policies, Aburime said it was impossible to know whether the President had offered such advice behind the scenes, noting that influence did not guarantee acceptance. Kanu’s release will be resolved politically On the continued detention of Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Nnamdi Kanu, Aburime said the matter had assumed a political dimension and would ultimately require a political resolution. Soludo had previously visited Kanu in detention and pledged to work towards securing his release. Asked why the governor had yet to achieve that objective despite his closeness and relationship with Tinubu, Aburime declined to comment extensively but said efforts towards a resolution were not over. “The Nnamdi Kanu case has become a political case and it will be resolved politically,” he said. Monday sit-at-home defeated, Anambra back to life Soludo declared that the enforcement of the Monday sit-at-home order by armed groups had been defeated, with commercial and social activities returning to normal across Anambra. He said vehicles were moving freely and major centres, including Awka, Onitsha and Nnewi were bustling with activities. “The war has been conquered, and all the debris is buried,” he said, insisting that residents could now move around freely and that Anambra was back to life. END The post Igbo must unite, build alliances to produce president — Soludo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2026/27 Ghana League: Vision end winless run with 3-1 victory over Dreams
items.description: Vision FC ended a six-game winless run in the Ghana Premier League with a convincing 3-1 victory over Dreams FC at the Tuba AstroTurf on Sunday. The visitors made a flying start to the match, scoring three goals in the opening 26 minutes to secure their second win of the 2026/27 campaign. Sherif Mohammed opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Setsofia Agetey doubled Vision’s advantage five minutes later. Mohammed then completed his brace in the 26th minute to give Vision a commanding 3-0 lead before the break. Dreams FC responded in the second half, pulling one back in the 58th minute through an own goal by Ibrahim Larbi. However, Vision held on to claim all three points and end their disappointing run since winning their opening league fixture. The result leaves Dreams FC rooted to the bottom of the league table with three points after eight matches, having recorded three draws and five defeats without a win this season. Vision, meanwhile, move to ninth place with nine points from eight matches. They have now recorded two wins, three draws and three defeats. The victory provides a timely boost for Vision as they seek to build momentum in the league, while Dreams FC face mounting pressure to turn their fortunes around after another disappointing outing.

items.title: 6 terrorists killed, 2 soldiers martyred during Dera Ismail Khan IBO: ISPR
items.description: Security forces killed six terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan district, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday. The IBO was conducted on Saturday in DI Khan’s general area of Zarkani on the “reported presence of khawarij belonging to Indian proxy Fitna Al Khawarij ”, the military’s media affairs wing said in a statement . Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). “Owing to [the] meticulous conduct of operation by security forces, six India-sponsored khawarij were sent to hell,” ISPR said. It added that 36-year-old Naik Ghulam Murtaza, who hailed from Punjab’s Gujrat, and 30-year-old Sepoy Taseer Ahmed, a resident of Punjab’s Talagang, “fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifices and embraced martyrdom”. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed terrorists, who “remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies, as well as the killing of innocent civilians”, the ISPR statement noted. A sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other terrorist found in the area, ISPR said. It affirmed that the “relentless counterterrorism campaign under vision ‘ Azm-i- Istehkam ’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan ) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”. “These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation at all costs,” the military’s media wing stated. Surge in terrorism KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). In response to these incidents, security forces have been conducting operations in various parts of the province. Earlier this month, security forces killed eight terrorists during an IBO in DI Khan, state media reported, citing security sources. On Friday, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir affirmed that the armed forces will continue the counterterrorism campaign against India-sponsored terrorist groups “to the fullest”, vowing to “hit them hard wherever they are”. CDF Munir visited the Corps Headquarters in Peshawar, where he was briefed on the security situation, ongoing counterterrorism operations, border management measures and the operational preparedness of formations deployed in the province. According to a report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recorded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, reversing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters. Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period.

items.title: Kloto : La secrétaire générale du MCLD échange avec les membres de Kpalimé sur les fondamentaux du mouvement
items.description: Kpalimé, 25 oct. (ATOP) – La secrétaire générale du Mouvement pour le développement piloté par les communautés (MCLD), Gunjan Veda a échangé, le samedi 24 octobre à Kpalimé avec les membres du Développement piloté par la communauté (DPC), sur les valeurs fondamentales de l’organisation. Cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre de son séjour au Togo pour une formation internationale des formateurs sur l’outil d’évaluation participatif du développement piloté par les communautés. Selon Gunjan Veda, cette démarche repose sur la conviction que chaque être humain possède des connaissances, des compétences et un pouvoir d’action susceptible de contribuer à la transformation de sa communauté. « Chaque homme a la dignité de s’exprimer et de dire des choses qui concernent sa vie et la manière dont il peut changer pour de meilleures conditions de vie », a-t-elle souligné, mettant en avant la nécessité de replacer les populations au centre des décisions qui les concernent. La secrétaire générale a souligné que le mouvement entend ainsi encourager les communautés à renouer avec leurs propres ressources et savoirs. Elle a estimé que certaines perceptions héritées de la colonisation ont contribué à éloigner les populations de leurs capacités et de leur potentiel de développement. Pour la secrétaire générale du MCLD, le développement durable passe donc par la reconnaissance de la dignité humaine, la valorisation des connaissances locales et la participation des populations à la définition de leur avenir. S’adressant aux membres du mouvement à Kpalimé, la représentante du MCLD les a exhortés à croire en leurs valeurs, en leur intelligence et en leurs capacités à impulser le changement au sein de leurs communautés. Elle a insisté sur l’importance de la mise en commun des savoirs et des compétences individuelles, estimant que la transformation sociale ne peut se réaliser sans l’engagement des populations elles-mêmes. « Personne ne peut venir faire notre développement, Sinon nous-mêmes », a-t-elle affirmé, invitant les membres à unir leurs efforts pour construire des communautés capables de prendre en charge leur propre développement. Présent dans près de 40 pays et fort de plus de 3 000 membres, le MCLD est un mouvement international qui vise à renforcer les communautés pour qu’elles prennent en main leur développement à travers une gouvernance participative, inclusive et durable. Le MCLD intervient entre autres dans la gouvernance participative, l’autonomisation des communautés, l’égalité de genre, la paix et la cohésion sociale, le plaidoyer et les politiques publiques et le développement durable. ATOP/AYH/HKM

items.title: 2026/27 GPL: Swedru All Blacks beat Young Apostles to secure 2-1 win
items.description: Swedru All Blacks secured a 2-1 victory over Young Apostles in their Ghana Premier League Matchday 8 encounter, scoring twice in the second half. The visitors came close to opening the scoring in the 10th minute when Akoto Osae unleashed a powerful effort, but Young Apostles goalkeeper Osman Wahabu parried the ball before it was cleared away. The first half also saw a lengthy stoppage after goalkeeper Michael Appiah sustained an injury. Nine minutes of added time were played, but neither side could find the breakthrough before the interval. Swedru All Blacks eventually took the lead in the 55th minute through William Dankwah, who put the visitors 1-0 ahead. Young Apostles made a double substitution in the 62nd minute, with Solomon Ayikabia and Godfred Yartey replacing Eric Wiafe Darkwah and John Andoh as they sought to get back into the game. Yartey showed attacking intent in the 76th minute, taking on two opposing defenders, although his effort resulted in a throw-in. The substitute, however, made a decisive impact six minutes later when he scored in the 82nd minute to double Swedru All Blacks’ advantage. Illiasu grabbed a consolation in the 89th minute, but time had run out for the homesters. The visitors made triple substitutions, bringing on Andrews Quainoo, Vincent Baah Junior, Zayat Bubakari are in to replace Salisu Mohammed, Faisal Charwetey and Michael Abrokwah to protect their lead as they held on to secure a 2-1 win and claim all three points in the Matchday 8 fixture.

items.title: Kloto /Agroécologie : l’Union des coopératives des femmes du canton de Yokélé, lauréate du ‘’Prix du public Benoît Maria’’
items.description: Kpalimé, 25 oct. (ATOP) – L’Union des coopératives de femmes du canton de Yokélé (UCOFECY) a remporté le ‘’Prix du public Benoît Maria’’ pour l’agroécologie édition 2026, grâce à son centre de formation à l’agroécologie, a annoncé les responsables de l’Union le samedi 24 octobre à Kpalimé. Créé en 2022 par l’ONG Agronomes et vétérinaires sans frontières (AVSF), le Prix Benoît Maria pour l’agroécologie paysanne est une distinction internationale qui récompense les initiatives innovantes portées par des organisations paysannes en Afrique et en Amérique latine. Il rend hommage à Benoît Maria, ingénieur agronome et représentant d’AVSF au Guatemala, assassiné le 10 août 2020 alors qu’il défendait les droits des communautés autochtones et paysannes. Attribuée tous les deux ans, cette distinction vise à valoriser et à soutenir les initiatives paysannes qui contribuent au développement de pratiques agroécologiques durables. Elle vient récompenser les initiatives de cette organisation féminine qui œuvre dans la production agricole, la transformation des produits locaux et la promotion de l’autonomisation économique des femmes. Le ‘’Prix du public Benoît Maria’’ pour l’agroécologie constitue la troisième distinction de cette édition, après le Grand Prix du jury, décerné à l’association Olouguelemo du Mali pour ses actions de restauration des sols et de lutte contre l’érosion et la désertification dans la région de Bandiagara et le Prix d’honneur du jury attribué à l’association Tikapallana du Pérou pour son marché paysan mensuel consacré à l’agroécologie, organisé et géré par des femmes à Tambobamba. La présidente de l’Union, Avossé Abra Clémentine, a souligné que UCOFECY créée en 2018, est composée de quatre coopératives féminines, Gbenodou, Akofa, Goto et INGREED. Basée à Yokélé, elle intervient notamment dans le maraîchage, la production de soja, la culture du gingembre, la fabrication d’huile rouge et d’huile de palmiste, la production de savons locaux ainsi que l’élevage. Ces activités, dit-il, contribuent à la valorisation des ressources locales et au renforcement des moyens de subsistance des femmes membres. A travers son centre de formation à l’agroécologie, l’Union renforce les capacités des femmes et promeut des pratiques agricoles respectueuses de l’environnement. Cette orientation s’inscrit dans une dynamique de développement agricole durable, de valorisation des produits locaux et d’amélioration des conditions de vie des communautés rurales. ATOP/AYH/BA

items.title: 2026 U17 WWC: Nothing is tough for Black Maidens – Seidatu Wahab
items.description: Player of the Match, Seidatu Wahab, says the Black Maidens came into the Canada game with only one thing on their minds — victory. The midfield enforcer, who led by example in Ghana’s 2-0 win over Canada to send the Maidens into the Round of 16, admitted she has been down in recent matches but saved her best for the qualification decider. “I’m really excited. Lately, in my matches, I have been down, but this is the final game. Not the final, but this is the qualification match, so I have to bring my all out,” Wahab said. “The match was really tough, but I have to show I’m a leader. So, I brought all what I have in me. We really came for a win. That’s the only thing we came for. No draw, no loss, but a win.” The combative midfielder, who bossed the middle of the park against Canada, said the Maidens thrive under pressure. “It was really a tough game, but nothing is really tough for the Maidens,” she added. Wahab reserved special praise for her support system. “I would like to thank my best friend. Yeah, she’s the person I really thank, and my parents too. My teammates, they really helped me.” Wahab was named Player of the Match after Ghana’s 2-0 victory over Canada, with goals from Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku sealing Ghana’s place in the Round of 16 where they will face Argentina on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

items.title: Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss
items.description: Michael Carrick said he will do what is best for Manchester United after a 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth plunged his future as manager into doubt on Sunday. Winless in eight games in all competitions, the 20-time English champions slipped to within one point of the relegation zone after a damaging defeat at Old Trafford. “It’s a tough situation,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “What is next? I don’t know. “I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along, I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility, but we’ll have to wait and see.” Despite a dismal run of results, the United fans largely supported Carrick as he made his way off the field at full-time before they turned on the club’s players. “I have mixed emotions to have that connection with the supporters in the moment we’re in. I need time to digest that,” added Carrick. “I appreciate their support but the situation is where it’s at. We haven’t been good enough.” Carrick’s decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench and not even introduce the Portuguese international as a substitute backfired. Fernandes, last season’s Premier League player of the year, had criticised Carrick’s tactics after a 4-1 thrashing by Como on Wednesday. “There’s always times in games when you are trying to change the course of the game and to make a difference,” said Carrick as he swerved questions on Fernandes’s absence. “Those were the decisions we made today.” The post Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2026 U17 WWC: Seidatu Wahab wins Player of the Match against Canada
items.description: Midfielder Seidatu Wahab was named Player of the Match after an outstanding performance in Ghana’s crucial 2-0 victory over Canada at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Wahab was the engine room of the Black Maidens side, breaking up play, winning duels, and keeping Ghana ticking with her composure on the ball. While goals from substitutes Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku grabbed the headlines, it was Wahab’s tireless work in midfield that allowed Ghana to dominate proceedings and secure the win that sent them through to the Round of 16. Partnering Jessica Appiah in the middle of the park, Wahab screened the back four superbly, denying Canada any space to play, and was instrumental in launching Ghana’s attacks. Her standout moment came in the first half with a perfectly timed last-ditch tackle to deny Canada a clear goalscoring opportunity, before playing a key role in the build-up to Ghana’s opener. The award caps a strong tournament for Wahab, who has grown in stature with each game, from the defeat to Norway, to the thrilling 3-3 draw with Brazil, and now the vital win over Canada. The Black Maidens will now turn their attention to the Round of 16, where Wahab will again be crucial to Coach Nana Joe Adarkwa’s plans.
