items.title: IMF delegation assesses TOR’s rehabilitation and financial recovery efforts
items.description: A delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has visited the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) to familiarise itself with the refinery’s operations, assess ongoing rehabilitation works and gain insight into management’s efforts to restore the facility to sustained operational and financial stability. The visit formed part of the IMF team’s engagements with relevant government authorities and selected state-owned enterprises in Ghana to gain a better understanding of their operations, financial positions, challenges and contributions to the national economy. The delegation was led by the IMF’s Ghana Resident Representative, Dr. Adrian Alter, while the TOR team was led by its Managing Director, Mr. Edmond Kombat, Esq. During a meeting with the delegation, Mr. Kombat outlined the operational and financial challenges inherited by the current management, as well as measures introduced since May 2025 to restore confidence in the refinery’s operations and revive its major processing plants. Addressing the delegation, Mr. Kombat emphasised that management had relied on internally generated funds to sustain the refinery’s operations since assuming office. “Since this new management took over, we have not received a dime from government. Every single thing is done through our internally generated funds,” Mr. Kombat said. He explained that management had prioritised financial discipline, operational improvements and the rehabilitation of critical facilities as part of efforts to reposition the refinery for long-term sustainability. Mr. Kombat disclosed that TOR was engaging the government over its outstanding debt obligations, with discussions focusing on possible restructuring and the reconciliation of historical financial commitments between the refinery and the state. According to him, TOR inherited a debt burden of approximately US$517 million, of which about US$120 million is owed to the government. “Out of the US$517 million debt we inherited, we owe about US$120 million to the government. We are trying to restructure our debt with the government,” he explained. The refinery is also engaging other state institutions to resolve outstanding financial obligations between TOR and the respective entities. Management is exploring possible netting-off arrangements to reconcile the obligations and establish the actual financial position of the parties involved. On the refinery’s financial performance, Mr. Kombat disclosed that TOR recorded a profit in the previous year, expressing optimism that the company could sustain profitability in the current and subsequent years. He attributed this positive outlook, in part, to improved macroeconomic stability and ongoing efforts to strengthen the refinery’s operational and financial position. As part of its long-term strategy, management is considering a potential listing of TOR on the Ghana Stock Exchange to attract investment and provide additional capital for the refinery’s operations and expansion. Mr. Kombat explained that a stock market listing could create opportunities for Ghanaian institutions and other investors to acquire shares in the company, providing an additional avenue for raising funds to support its recovery and growth. The IMF delegation also sought clarification on the volume of crude oil processed by TOR, particularly supplies sourced from Ghana’s domestic oil fields. In response, Mr. Kombat indicated that the refinery had processed approximately five million barrels of crude oil, including about two million barrels sourced from Ghanaian fields, with the remainder coming from external sources. He explained that TOR’s first domestic crude supply came from the Jubilee field through a transaction with Vitol, which was fully paid for. He also acknowledged the contribution of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC), which supplied its share of Ghana’s crude allocation to the refinery. “Our first domestic crude came from the Jubilee field through Vitol, and it was fully paid for. GNPC also gave us its portion of Ghana’s allocation,” Mr. Kombat stated. He further noted that Ghana produces approximately 38 million barrels of crude oil annually, with about 11 million barrels representing the government’s share. The Managing Director expressed hope that GNPC would make its full crude allocation available to TOR for refining by the following year. He said this would improve feedstock availability and support more consistent refinery operations. The delegation also sought to understand the impact of TOR’s resumption of operations on the Ghanaian economy and consumers. In response, Mr. Kombat highlighted the refinery’s contribution to domestic petroleum product availability, price stability, and the country’s ability to withstand disruptions in international petroleum markets. He explained that domestic refining could help reduce Ghana’s exposure to external supply shocks, particularly during periods of geopolitical tension and uncertainty in global oil markets, including the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. He also acknowledged government interventions aimed at cushioning consumers against the effects of changes in petroleum prices, noting the importance of maintaining a reliable domestic supply of petroleum products. Highlighting the refinery’s commercial potential, Mr. Kombat drew attention to TOR’s tank farm, storage infrastructure and product distribution network. He indicated that TOR has approximately one million metric tonnes of storage capacity, which is three times the capacity of the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company (BOST). The Managing Director further explained that TOR is connected to eight privately operated depots, enabling the refinery to pump petroleum products directly to those facilities. He said these arrangements provide additional revenue opportunities for the refinery, alongside other commercial activities, including laboratory services for petroleum product testing. The discussions also covered corporate governance and financial accountability, particularly efforts to clear a six-year backlog of unaudited accounts. Mr. Kombat explained that the Ghana Audit Service had undertaken the audit exercise to address the six-year backlog of outstanding accounts. He added that management intended to appoint an external audit firm at the refinery’s next Annual General Meeting (AGM) to undertake subsequent audits. KPMG had previously conducted audit assignments for the company. The Managing Director also briefed the delegation on improvements in financial reporting and internal controls, staff-related reforms, and measures to sustain crude supply for continued operations. He noted that these initiatives formed part of a broader management strategy to improve accountability, strengthen financial discipline and enhance operational efficiency. The IMF team was further briefed on ongoing efforts to increase the refinery’s processing capacity, rehabilitate other critical units and restore facilities required to support more reliable operations. These interventions are intended to strengthen TOR’s contribution to Ghana’s energy security, improve its financial sustainability and position it to play a more significant role in the country’s petroleum value chain. Following the discussions, the delegation toured parts of the refinery to observe rehabilitated facilities and ongoing engineering works. The tour provided the IMF team with an opportunity to gain first-hand insight into TOR’s operational environment, the progress made under the current management and the work that remains to be completed. Members of the delegation expressed appreciation for the engagement and the opportunity to gain a better understanding of the refinery’s operations and recovery efforts. The visit also provided a platform for TOR management to outline the measures being pursued to restore critical infrastructure, improve financial performance and strengthen the refinery’s contribution to Ghana’s energy security. The Tema Oil Refinery remains Ghana’s premier refinery, serving customers within the country and beyond its borders.

items.title: The nuclear danger at sea
items.description: Dawn’s October 23 editorial rightly warned about India’s nuclear-armed submarine patrols. The danger is larger than a new vessel at sea. It is a sea-based nuclear force growing alongside precision-strike capabilities, missile defence and a false confidence in initiating military action. Imagining that these developments confer a first-strike advantage or create a safe space for war is imprudent. Pakistan has the capability and resolve to preserve the strategic balance. Retired Lt-Gen Mazhar Jamil, Adviser to the National Command Authority, warned at the International Institute for Strategic Studies on October 13 that continuous at-sea deterrence further weakens the credibility of India’s declared no-first-use policy and points towards an offensive strike posture. He added that unannounced submarine-launched ballistic-missile tests, with operationalised weapons aboard submarines, raise the risks of misperception and escalation. Pakistan reserves the right to take all appropriate measures to protect its security and the regional balance. At the Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference a week later, retired Lt-Gen Khalid Kidwai, also an adviser to the National Command Authority, reinforced the warning, saying Pakistan would review its options if India sought to impose a strategic imbalance. In June 2026, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (Sipri) estimated that India had a stockpile of 190 nuclear warheads and 12 of these deployed on a nuclear-powered ballistic-missile submarine for occasional deterrence patrols. That estimate is too low and arrives seven years late. Prime Minister Modi announced the INS Arihant’s first deterrence patrol in 2018 and the Indian Navy again patrolled again during the 2019 crisis . India has three operational ballistic-missile submarines (SSBN), with a fourth expected in 2027. Next year, the four SSBNs will have a combined capacity to launch missiles carrying up to 72 warheads from 24 tubes. A larger fleet of 12 nuclear ballistic and attack submarines is envisaged in the 2030s . Aggressive posturing India’s professed no-first-use pledge cannot be judged without taking into account its capabilities and political conduct. A ready, concealed launch platform gains a different meaning when combined with counterforce ambitions, missile defence and talk of pre-emption. General Kidwai’s assessment about a possible strike at ‘zero notice’ should be read in that setting. Pakistan has never allowed its deterrence capability to be neutralised by India’s posture that is taken as routine modernisation. Strategic stability rests on a credible balance and Pakistan will maintain it under all circumstances. General Zubair Hayat, former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee, argued at the Islamabad Non-proliferation Conference that the old international order is giving way without an equitable replacement. His strategic point applies here: strategic exemptions for a favoured state, followed by alarm at its neighbour’s balancing measures, do not produce equal security. The nuclearisation of the Indian Ocean did not begin when Pakistan raised its concerns. It began with India’s risky choices, enabled and fuelled by an international tendency to treat its ambitions as benign. May 2025 demonstrated the danger of that assumption on land and in the air. On the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, President Asif Ali Zardari reiterated that India used Pahalgam’s false flag as a guise for premeditated strikes. India ignored Pakistan’s offer of a neutral investigation and had to endure a defeat and loss of face. Pakistan’s calibrated conventional response, under political authority, restored conventional deterrence, while Full Spectrum Deterrence preserved the strategic ceiling. The Indian Air Force grounded itself, and the Indian Navy’s carrier strike group cut a hasty retreat to safety. The ceasefire followed Islamabad’s response and New Delhi’s call for third-party mediation. There was no safe band of war then, and there is none at sea now. A lesson for India Retired Lt-Gen Sarfraz Sattar, who served as Director General of the Strategic Plans Division, has also warned that emerging technologies and great-power competition threaten nuclear stability. The March 2022 BrahMos launch into Pakistan showed why. A supersonic nuclear-capable missile crossed the border in peacetime; India waited nearly two days before acknowledging it and did not accept Pakistan’s call for a joint inquiry , raising the risk of escalation. Three years on, India carried that risk into wartime by employing BrahMos against another nuclear power — the first such instance . The sea-leg of India’s nuclear triad and dual-capable missiles are sinews of a Hindutva-inflected policy of hegemony and coercion. Pakistan’s declared Full Spectrum Deterrence covers the range of threats it faces, and it clearly signals that aggression at any level or in any domain risks a response that will deny objectives and impose costs; an adversary cannot dictate the level at which a confrontation will remain. Political authority, prepared forces and credible options give that warning its weight. As India’s posture changes, Pakistan will take the measures necessary to safeguard its sovereignty and strategic balance. Risk reduction has value, but it cannot substitute for deterrence or responsible political choices. Dialogue is worthwhile when it reduces the incentives and opportunities for unilateral force, not when it is offered as a substitute for Pakistan’s defence. Pakistan always stands ready to impose greater costs for any misadventure that India may undertake, including in the maritime domain. In May 2025, Islamabad demonstrated that its calibrated notch-up response should not be read to mean that every aggression will meet the same ceiling. General Kidwai also recommended adding a “ plus ” to Pakistan’s quid-pro-quo plus response strategy. The lesson for India is direct. Neither an expanding submarine fleet nor other developments give it an edge over Pakistan’s response to aggression. Pakistan has demonstrated both resolve and the means to defend itself. It will preserve the balance on which peace depends. In the Subcontinent, the true enemy is the delusion that war can be kept safely on a lower rung. That Indian aspiration makes the unthinkable look controllable. It’s an illusion that a war can be started low, kept low, and stopped on command. A political choice driven by Hindutva and Akhand Bharat may begin the escalation; interaction decides where it goes. Field Marshal Asim Munir expressed the governing reality most aptly: there is no space for war in a nuclearised environment.

items.title: Safi : les recherches se poursuivent pour retrouver un bateau de pêche traditionnel et ses cinq marins
items.description: Les opérations de recherche et de ratissage se poursuivent au large de Safi pour retrouver le bateau de pêche traditionnel « Lalla Khadija », porté disparu avec cinq marins à bord, après un retard inhabituel de son retour au port. Les recherches mobilisent d’importants moyens maritimes et aériens, dans un contexte de conditions météorologiques et maritimes difficiles. Dans un communiqué, le ministère délégué auprès du ministre de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et du Développement rural, chargé de la Pêche maritime, indique que ses services compétents ont été alertés le vendredi 23 octobre 2026, à 17 heures, par l’armateur du bateau, immatriculé sous le numéro 7-7016, signalant que l’embarcation n’était pas rentrée au port de Safi dans les délais habituels. À la suite de cette alerte, des opérations de recherche ont été immédiatement lancées dans la zone maritime susceptible d’abriter le bateau, sous la supervision du Centre de coordination des opérations de recherche et de sauvetage maritimes de Bouznika. Celui-ci a alerté les différentes embarcations et les navires de commerce présents dans la zone ou en transit, afin d’accélérer les recherches et de localiser le bateau. Le dispositif a été renforcé par la participation des deux vedettes de sauvetage des ports de Safi et d’Agadir, ainsi que de plusieurs bateaux de pêche et navires commerciaux, dont certains ont été déroutés vers la zone de recherche. Deux hélicoptères, relevant respectivement de la Gendarmerie royale et de la Marine royale, ont également été mobilisés. Ils ont effectué plusieurs sorties aériennes de ratissage afin de tenter de repérer l’embarcation disparue. À l’heure de la publication du communiqué, les opérations se poursuivent avec la mobilisation des moyens maritimes et aériens, civils et militaires, sous la coordination du centre de Bouznika. L’objectif demeure de localiser le bateau et de porter secours aux cinq membres de son équipage, malgré les conditions météorologiques et maritimes difficiles dans la zone. Le ministère assure que les recherches se poursuivent en coordination avec l’ensemble des intervenants et que tous les moyens disponibles sont mobilisés pour retrouver l’embarcation et son équipage. Il indique également qu’il tiendra l’opinion publique informée de l’évolution de la situation, dès que de nouvelles informations confirmées seront disponibles. The post Safi : les recherches se poursuivent pour retrouver un bateau de pêche traditionnel et ses cinq marins appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Visas pour la France : Capago Algérie exige le code QR
items.description: Capago Algérie exige des demandeurs de visas pour la France à se munir de la confirmation de rendez-vous qui comporte désormais un code QR. « Avant de vous présenter au centre, veillez à vous munir de votre confirmation de rendez-vous. Celle-ci comporte un code QR qui vous sera demandé à votre arrivée », a indiqué le prestataire sur sa page Facebook ce dimanche 25 octobre. La confirmation peut être présentée directement sur « votre téléphone ou en version imprimée. Dans les deux cas, le code QR doit être clairement lisible », a ajouté Capago Algérie. Capago Algérie : le code QR est obligatoire « Nous vous invitons à vérifier la présence du QR avant votre déplacement au centre », insiste l’opérateur en charge de la réception des demandes de visa pour la France. Copago Algérie a introduit ces dernières semaines des changements « provisoires » dans la procédure de demande de visa. Il s’agit de la confirmation automatique des rendez-vous mise en œuvre depuis le 7 octobre dernier. Il a été procédé au changement du mode de règlement des frais de visa qui se fait, depuis le 7 octobre également, par espèce, le jour de dépôt du dossier. Copago Algérie avait mis en place, en juin dernier, un service de « pré-vérification des documents » qui permet aux demandeurs de visa Schengen de sécuriser leurs dossiers et de leur éviter de se rendre au centre avec des dossiers incomplets. La France a délivré un peu plus de 204 000 visas aux ressortissants algériens, au cours de l’année 2025. L’article Visas pour la France : Capago Algérie exige le code QR est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Musk affirme avoir bloqué l'utilisation de Starlink pour des frappes de drones ukrainiennes
items.description: Le 24 octobre, Elon Musk a accuse les forces ukrainiennes d'avoir enfreint les regles d'utilisation de Starlink pour mener des frappes offensives a l'aide de drones. Dans un message publie sur X, le fondateur de SpaceX a indique que cette utilisation du reseau satellitaire avait ete bloquee la semaine precedente. Correct. Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be. Starshield, a different system, is controlled by the US government. What they decide to do is up to them. Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week. Starlink remains critical to the defense of Ukraine, as it is the only system that cannot be jammed or blown up, at least for now. Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact. Starlink was also crucial to preventing Russia from overrunning Ukraine in the early days of the war, as all other means of communication were destroyed or jammed by Russia. SpaceX has done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth BY FAR. That said, I have nothing but UTTER CONTEMPT for the virtue-signaling evil warmongers who push for endless slaughter and offer no realistic solution to the conflict. May you burn in hell. End of story. — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 24, 2026 « Les militaires ukrainiens ont viole les conditions d'utilisation de Starlink et s'en sont servis pour mener des frappes offensives a l'aide de drones dans le but de tuer des personnes. Cette faille a ete fermee la semaine derniere », a declare Elon Musk. L'entrepreneur a souligne que Starlink est un service commercial de communications satellitaires dont l'utilisation pour de telles attaques n'a jamais ete autorisee. Il l'a distingue de Starshield, un systeme destine notamment a des usages militaires et place, selon lui, sous le controle du gouvernement americain. Des restrictions qui perturbent les operations de Kiev Ces declarations interviennent apres plusieurs perturbations signalees par les forces ukrainiennes depuis la nuit du 14 octobre. Certains terminaux auraient perdu leur connexion au-dela de 160 km/h, compliquant le pilotage des drones, le ravitaillement des unites et plusieurs operations militaires. Les restrictions ont rapidement suscite des tensions entre Kiev et Washington . Le 18 octobre, Volodymyr Zelensky a accuse l'administration de Donald Trump d'avoir limite l'acces aux communications satellitaires, tout en reconnaissant ignorer qui avait pris cette decision. Le president americain a dementi toute implication. Selon The Economist , Elon Musk aurait ordonne ces restrictions en reaction aux frappes ukrainiennes contre des raffineries de petrole russes. Cette version, qui etablit un lien entre les limitations du reseau et les attaques visant les infrastructures energetiques russes, n'a toutefois pas ete confirmee par l'entrepreneur. Le 24 octobre, les autorites ukrainiennes ont annonce le retablissement des communications a des vitesses normales. Elon Musk a neanmoins maintenu que la possibilite d'utiliser le service commercial Starlink pour mener des frappes offensives avait ete bloquee. Musk met en avant la dependance militaire de l'Ukraine Les accusations du patron de SpaceX ont ete contestees a Kiev. L'ancien conseiller du ministere ukrainien de la Defense, Sergueï Sternenko, affirme que les drones necessitant une liaison satellitaire devaient utiliser Starshield et non le service commercial Starlink. Selon lui, ce dernier ne pouvait donc pas etre employe pour ces operations. Musk a cependant insiste sur le role determinant de son reseau pour les forces ukrainiennes. « Si Starlink etait desactive, le front ukrainien s'effondrerait immediatement. Ce n'est pas une menace, mais un simple constat », a-t-il declare sur X le 24 octobre. Le milliardaire a egalement critique les partisans d'une poursuite des combats qui, selon lui, ne proposent aucune solution realiste pour mettre fin au conflit. La question de l'utilisation militaire de Starlink a egalement suscite une reaction a Moscou. Le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, a estime qu'il serait preferable que des technologies aussi avancees ne soient pas employees a des fins militaires.

items.title: Igboho seeks wider security role for traditional rulers
items.description: …unveils 20,000 Iru Ekun volunteers in Oyo …links Abuja trip to strengthening regional security network By Adeola Badru Yoruba nation activist, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has called for a stronger security role for traditional rulers across the South-West, declaring that the Iru Ekun Security Network, which he described as the brainchild of the region’s traditional institutions, has attracted 20,000 volunteers in Oyo State. Igboho made the declaration on Sunday at the launch of the network at the popular Mapo Hall in Ibadan, where he explained that his recent visit to Abuja was aimed at strengthening the organisation’s security responsibilities and expanding its effectiveness in protecting communities. The development was on the heels of the persistent security concerns across Nigeria, including abductions, killings and other criminal activities, which have placed renewed emphasis on cooperation between traditional institutions, local communities and conventional security agencies. According to a statement issued by Igboho’s media office, no fewer than 20,000 volunteers joined the organisation in Oyo State, with its operational reach extending across Yorubaland and parts of Kwara and Niger states. The statement said the Oyo launch followed similar inaugurations in Osun, Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun and Ondo states, alongside engagements with traditional rulers and community leaders. It added that the organisation had collaborated with the Nigerian Army, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to tackle abductions, killings and other forms of insecurity, particularly in the South-West. Commending the turnout at the Ibadan launch, Igboho said the participation of the volunteers demonstrated the willingness of residents to contribute to the safety of their communities, regardless of ethnic, religious or political differences. “The impressive development represents a milestone which indicates genuine interest of Oyo people in active participation to ensure safety and security of residents, irrespective of tribes, religion and political affiliations,” he said. Explaining the purpose of his Abuja trip, Igboho said the engagement was aimed at advancing the responsibilities of the security network, which he maintained was established through the initiative of traditional rulers in the South-West. “I was in Abuja this morning so that Iru Ekun’s security responsibilities can be further strengthened.“ “This is because Iru Ekun is the brain child of South West traditional rulers and it will continue to serve its purpose for the peace and effective security of our communities,” he said. He disclosed that the trip followed an invitation he received the previous night and linked the engagement to his collaboration with the Olubadan of Ibadanland. “I received the call last night to come to Abuja. My Abuja trip was as a result of the collaboration with our traditional ruler, the Olubadan of Ibadanland,” he stated. Igboho also expressed gratitude to God for what he described as protection against banditry, while acknowledging the contributions of traditional rulers to peace and security across the country. “Firstly I want to thank Almighty God who has all powers, owns us, preserves us. The God that says we won’t be overcomed by bandits. We thank God,” he said. He added: “After that, we thank all traditional rulers in Nigeria and may God grant them a long life.” The activist subsequently commended President Bola Tinubu, whom he credited with providing a platform for members of the initiative to interact and pursue their security objectives. “We are also paying homage to the person, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who provided this platform so that we can interact as Iru Ekun members,” he said. Addressing the volunteers, Igboho expressed concern over what he described as the contemptuous attitude of some people towards them, predicting that their efforts would eventually attract recognition. “Some people are still taking a despicable look at you (Volunteers). Soon they will lobby you for positions,” he remarked. Meanwhile, Igboho urged Nigerians, including members of the Iru Ekun Security Network, to support Tinubu’s re-election bid and vote for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the forthcoming January presidential election. items.title: Isak extends hot streak as Liverpool sink Brighton
items.description: Alexander Isak extended his hot streak in Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday as Reds boss Andoni Iraola savoured his first Premier League victory at Anfield. Iraola’s side struck twice in quick succession in the first half, with Pascal Gross’s own goal followed by Isak’s latest strike. Isak has netted six times in seven league games this season and has three goals in his last four matches. After a turbulent debut season following his acrimonious move from Newcastle, the Sweden striker is finally beginning to repay his £125 million ($167 million) fee. It was a welcome first taste of top-flight success at Anfield for Iraola, who had failed to win his first three league games on Merseyside since arriving from Bournemouth in the close season. The Spaniard, who had won Champions League and League Cup games at Anfield, has led Liverpool to four successive victories in all competitions since the chastening 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City. Liverpool have climbed to fourth place, just one point behind third-placed Brighton after inflicting the high-flying Seagulls’ second league loss this term. The Reds are six points behind leaders City as they eye a potential title challenge. Liverpool were winless in their previous five home league matches dating back to last season, drawing four times and losing once. But they put Brighton to the sword in composed fashion, stopping the visitors’ recent goal blitz after they arrived at Anfield as the league’s top scorers. Brighton should have taken an early lead when Diego Gomez’s pass caught out Virgil van Dijk and Gross crossed to Yasin Ayari, who fired wastefully over with the goal at his mercy. – Rampant Reds – Liverpool took full advantage of that escape to open the scoring in the 17th minute. Ronald Araujo’s buccaneering run and cross into the Brighton area picked out Florian Wirtz for a powerful strike that took a hefty deflection off Gross as it whistled into the bottom corner. Cody Gakpo nearly doubled Liverpool’s lead moments later with a rising drive that Bart Verbruggen tipped over. Liverpool were rampant and it was no surprise when Isak bagged their second goal in the 21st minute. Iraola opted for Bradley Barcola and Gakpo on the flanks despite Rio Ngumoha’s virtuoso performance in the midweek win against Villarreal. And Barcola repaid that faith when he sprinted onto a long pass from Reds keeper Alisson Becker and guided a cross into Isak for a clinical close-range finish. Isak has scored in three consecutive league appearances for the first time since January 2025 for Newcastle. He was denied a fourth by Lewis Dunk’s last-ditch block after the Sweden striker took aim from Wirtz’s pass. Liverpool kept pushing and Araujo’s blast forced a superb save from Verbruggen just before half-time. The announcement that Liverpool’s troubled rivals Manchester United were losing to Bournemouth brought huge cheers from the Kop at the interval. It was that kind of day for Liverpool, who comfortably held their lead in the second half despite losing Wirtz to an injury. Iraola’s men are hitting their stride after an inconsistent start to the season. Now come a pair of intriguing tests as Chelsea visit Anfield in the League Cup fourth round on Wednesday before second-placed Arsenal arrive for a crucial clash on November 1. The post Isak extends hot streak as Liverpool sink Brighton appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: «Stupide» : Poutine critique la politique européenne envers Moscou
items.description: Vladimir Poutine a qualifie de « stupide », ce 25 octobre, la politique de l'Union europeenne visant a se detourner des produits et des ressources russes. Dans un entretien accorde au journaliste Pavel Zaroubine, le president russe a reproche aux dirigeants europeens d'avoir renonce a des ressources energetiques bon marche, tout en reduisant l'acces de leurs entreprises au marche russe, un debouche commercial important. Le chef de l'etat a insiste sur le fait que la Russie n'a jamais refuse de fournir du petrole, du gaz, du charbon ou de l'uranium aux pays europeens. Il a ainsi attribue la reduction des echanges energetiques aux decisions prises par ces memes gouvernements europeens. Malgre ces restrictions, les approvisionnements russes se poursuivent, le gaz naturel liquefie (GNL) russe representant encore 20 % du marche europeen du GNL. Cette politique a egalement pese sur les relations commerciales, a poursuivi le president russe. Il a explique que certaines entreprises europeennes avaient dû quitter la Russie sous la pression de leurs gouvernements, alors qu'elles souhaitaient poursuivre leurs activites. D'autres sont toutefois restees sur le marche russe, ou Moscou s'efforce, selon lui, de leur garantir des conditions favorables. Endettement et recul industriel : Poutine souligne les difficultes europeennes Le president russe a egalement mis en lumiere les difficultes economiques de plusieurs pays europeens, notamment leur dette publique et leurs deficits budgetaires. Il a cite l'Italie, dont la dette publique atteint pres de 139 % du PIB, contre 17,5 % pour la Russie. Il a egalement evoque la dette exterieure russe equivalente a 2,6 % du PIB. Vladimir Poutine a par ailleurs insiste sur les deficits budgetaires de la France et de la Belgique, qui atteindraient respectivement 5,1 % et 5,2 % du PIB. Il a juge ces niveaux particulierement eleves, mettant en garde contre leurs consequences pour les economies concernees. a ces difficultes budgetaires s'ajoute le recul de la production industrielle europeenne. Vladimir Poutine a qualifie de « dramatique » la baisse enregistree depuis 2021 de plusieurs grandes economies du continent. Il a notamment cite l'Allemagne, premiere economie de l'Union europeenne, dont les difficultes industrielles se repercutent, selon lui, sur l'ensemble de la zone euro. Crise migratoire et tensions sociales en Europe Vladimir Poutine a egalement aborde la crise migratoire, soulignant les difficultes des etats europeens a assurer l'assimilation des migrants installes depuis plusieurs annees ainsi que de leurs enfants. Selon lui, les autorites ne disposent pas des moyens necessaires pour repondre a ces besoins, notamment en matiere d'education et de transmission des coutumes et traditions locales. Enfin, le president russe a rejete les accusations attribuant a Moscou un role dans les troubles et les mouvements de protestation observes dans plusieurs grandes villes europeennes. Il les a jugees manifestement exagerees, estimant que la Russie etait une nouvelle fois designee comme responsable des difficultes rencontrees en Europe. Vladimir Poutine a toutefois souligne que Moscou ne se rejouissait pas de ces evenements, tout en affirmant la necessite de repondre aux accusations portees contre son pays.

items.title: ONU : la candidature émiratie de Lana Nusseibeh suscite des critiques
items.description: Les emirats arabes unis ont officiellement propose, le 21 octobre, la candidature de Lana Nusseibeh au poste de secretaire general des Nations unies (ONU). Cette diplomate, actuellement secretaire d'etat au ministere emirati des Affaires etrangeres et ancienne representante permanente de son pays aupres de l'organisation, figure parmi les pretendants a la succession d'António Guterres, dont le second mandat prend fin le 31 decembre. Cette candidature intervient alors qu'aucun favori ne s'est clairement degage dans la course a la direction de l'organisation internationale. Mais le choix d'Abou Dhabi a rapidement suscite des critiques, en particulier en raison des accusations de soutien emirati aux Forces de soutien rapide (FSR), impliquees dans la guerre civile soudanaise. Les autorites emiraties ont toujours rejete ces accusations. Une diplomate experimentee au cœur des critiques Lana Nusseibeh connaît les mecanismes diplomatiques des Nations unies. Elle a represente les emirats arabes unis aupres de l'organisation de 2013 a 2024, notamment durant le mandat de son pays au Conseil de securite en 2022 et 2023. Son parcours l'a placee au cœur des relations diplomatiques d'Abou Dhabi, notamment dans le cadre du rapprochement avec Israel. Pour ses detracteurs, cette experience souleve toutefois des interrogations sur l'independance dont elle pourrait faire preuve a la tete de l'ONU. Cameron Hudson, ancien analyste de la CIA specialise dans l'Afrique et ex-responsable des affaires africaines au Conseil de securite nationale americain, accuse la diplomate d'avoir contribue a la strategie d'influence emiratie au sein de l'organisation, notamment sur les dossiers susceptibles de mettre en cause son pays. Ces critiques s'inscrivent dans un contexte de controverses autour de la guerre au Soudan, ou plusieurs enquetes et rapports ont mis en cause le role presume des emirats dans le soutien aux FSR. Abou Dhabi dement fournir un appui militaire a cette faction. Les accusations et les dementis constituent ainsi un enjeu majeur du debat autour de la candidature emiratie. Une election soumise au Conseil de securite Lana Nusseibeh est la septieme candidate annoncee dans la course a la succession d'António Guterres. Pour etre recommande a l'Assemblee generale, le futur secretaire general doit obtenir le soutien d'au moins neuf des 15 membres du Conseil de securite, sans veto de l'un des cinq membres permanents : les etats-Unis, la Chine, la France, le Royaume-Uni et la Russie. La possibilite de voir une femme acceder pour la premiere fois a ce poste constitue egalement un enjeu de cette selection. D'autres candidatures, notamment latino-americaines, sont evoquees dans le cadre d'un processus marque par des equilibres geographiques et diplomatiques. Pour Mira Al-Hussein, sociologue emiratie a l'universite d'edimbourg, l'election de Lana Nusseibeh renforcerait l'influence internationale des emirats arabes unis et leur capacite a peser sur les decisions multilaterales. D'autres observateurs redoutent qu'un tel choix ne souleve des questions sur la neutralite de l'institution, chargee notamment de promouvoir la paix, les droits fondamentaux et le respect du droit international.

items.title: Le Forum des médias Russie-Afrique organisé par RT réunira à Moscou des représentants de 46 pays africains du 26 au 29 octobre
items.description: a l'initiative de RT, Moscou accueillera du 26 au 29 octobre le Forum des medias Russie-Afrique, organise avec la participation de Sputnik et de TASS. Plus de 200 invites issus de 46 pays africains feront le deplacement dans la capitale russe, parmi lesquels des responsables de medias, des personnalites politiques, des experts et des blogueurs. Les echanges porteront sur le role des medias dans le developpement et l'unite de l'Afrique, ainsi que sur leur contribution a l'affirmation de l'identite africaine et a la representation du continent a l'etranger. Le forum reunira ainsi des professionnels russes et africains autour des principaux enjeux du secteur. Plusieurs personnalites africaines sont attendues, notamment Gregoire Ndjaka, directeur general de l'Union africaine de radiodiffusion, et evariste Ngamana, ministre de la Communication et des Medias de la Republique centrafricaine. Parmi les intervenants russes figurent egalement Elizaveta Brodskaïa, premiere redactrice en chef adjointe de RT, Dmitri Kisselev, directeur general du groupe Rossiya Segodnya, et Andreï Kondrachov, directeur general de TASS. Quatre jours d'echanges et de cooperation russo-africaine Les 26 et 27 octobre, le Centre national « Russie », a Moscou, accueillera les premieres sessions du forum. RT y reunira des dirigeants de grandes chaînes de television africaines ainsi que des blogueurs africains comptant au moins un million d'abonnes. Rossiya Segodnya et TASS organiseront egalement leurs propres sessions. Le 28 octobre, les travaux se poursuivront au Gostiny Dvor, ou une seance pleniere rassemblera les dirigeants de RT, de Rossiya Segodnya et de TASS, ainsi que des representants des autorites russes et africaines chargees du secteur des medias. La derniere journee, le 29 octobre, sera notamment consacree a une rencontre organisee par RT avec les descendants de plusieurs grandes figures de l'histoire africaine, dont Nelson Mandela, Patrice Lumumba, Samora Machel et Gamal Abdel Nasser. Cette session s'inscrira dans le cadre du projet televise de RT « Afrique : l'heritage des grands » ( African Legacy ). Des sessions de Rossiya Segodnya et de TASS sont egalement prevues au Gostiny Dvor. Outre les debats, le programme prevoit des emissions conjointes entre les participants africains et les medias russes, ainsi que la signature de plusieurs accords de cooperation avec la partie russe. En amont du forum, les invites etrangers ont egalement ete convies a un programme culturel prevu les 24 et 25 octobre, comprenant des visites de lieux emblematiques de Moscou.

items.title: Casses en France : une usine Framatome, produisant un métal «stratégique», cambriolée pour la sixième fois en sept ans
items.description: La France en libre-service ? En plus des musees ou des donnees personnelles , et plus recemment des commerces , les usines Seveso n'echappent visiblement pas a la convoitise de voleurs. Selon Le Dauphine Libere qui a revele l'affaire, « plusieurs centaines de kilos de cristaux d'hafnium, representant une valeur de plusieurs millions d'euros », ont ete voles dans l'usine Framatome de Jarrie (Isere), classee Seveso seuil haut, dans la nuit du 21 au 22 octobre. Vol qui aurait ete «commis vers 3h du matin », a precise le quotidien regional. « Un interimaire – car l'usine fonctionne jour et nuit – s'est d'ailleurs retrouve nez a nez avec les malfaiteurs avant de s'enfuir pour se refugier au poste de garde », peut-on lire dans l'article d'Ici Isere, qui a confirme l'information du Dauphine Libere . La France premier producteur mondial d'hafnium Le quotidien a d'ailleurs epingle une question ecrite du depute Julien Brugerolles, publiee au Journal officiel a la mi-juin apres un casse similaire commis dans la nuit du 3 au 4 mai, selon laquelle il s'agirait ni plus ni moins que du sixieme vol depuis 2019 dans cette usine. Ce metal rare, provenant de l'epuration du zirconium – et dont la France est le premier producteur mondial, devant les etats-Unis –, entre notamment dans la construction de drones de combat et d'avions de chasse ou encore dans les systemes de propulsion de sous-marins nucleaires et de certains missiles. Fin septembre, Le Parisien rapportait que des gendarmes iserois avaient retrouve 150 kilos de cristaux d'hafnium ainsi que « plus de 500 000 euros et une arme de poing » au domicile d'un chef d'equipe de Framatome Jarrie, « visiblement friand de vehicules de luxe et de montres suisses ».

items.title: Algérie : les sénateurs approuvent l’envoi de militaires au Niger
items.description: Le Parlement algerien a franchi une etape importante dans le renforcement de la cooperation securitaire avec le Niger. Le Conseil de la nation, chambre haute du Parlement, a approuve a l'unanimite, le 25 octobre, une decision autorisant l'envoi d'unites militaires algeriennes a l'etranger, dans le cadre de la cooperation avec Niamey. Reunis en seance pleniere extraordinaire a huis clos, les senateurs ont ainsi donne leur feu vert a cette initiative, qui doit egalement etre soumise a l'Assemblee populaire nationale (APN), la chambre basse, pour approbation. Cette decision survient quatre jours apres la signature, le 21 octobre, d'un protocole d'accord visant a renforcer la cooperation militaire entre l'Algerie et le Niger. Le document a ete conclu a l'occasion de la visite a Alger du ministre nigerien de la Defense nationale, Salifou Mody. a cette occasion, le chef d'etat-major de l'Armee nationale populaire (ANP), le general d'armee Saïd Chanegriha, avait reaffirme la disponibilite de l'Algerie a examiner les propositions nigeriennes susceptibles de consolider la cooperation militaire et securitaire entre les deux pays. Le protocole prevoit notamment une cooperation et un echange d'experiences dans la lutte contre le terrorisme, ainsi qu'un soutien au renforcement des capacites operationnelles de l'armee nigerienne, en fonction des demandes des autorites du pays. La base de Madama evoquee pour un eventuel deploiement L'ancien diplomate algerien Amar Belani a evoque un possible deploiement des forces algeriennes sur la base militaire de Madama, dans le nord du Niger, a proximite de la frontiere libyenne. Selon lui, l'approbation parlementaire constitue une etape necessaire pour autoriser cet engagement dans le cadre de l'article 91 de la Constitution algerienne. Cette localisation hypothetique n'a toutefois pas ete confirmee officiellement dans les elements disponibles. La base de Madama occupe une position strategique dans une region marquee par les enjeux securitaires transfrontaliers et les activites de groupes armes. L'Algerie et le Niger partagent des preoccupations securitaires liees a la situation au Sahel et a la circulation de groupes armes dans les zones frontalieres. Le renforcement de leur cooperation militaire s'inscrit dans ce contexte regional. Une evolution du cadre constitutionnel algerien L'eventualite d'un deploiement militaire a l'etranger marque une evolution importante pour l'Algerie, dont la doctrine militaire a longtemps privilegie la defense du territoire national. La derniere participation de l'armee algerienne a un conflit hors de ses frontieres remonte a 1973, lorsque des forces algeriennes avaient pris part a la guerre arabo-israelienne. La revision constitutionnelle de 2020 a toutefois ouvert la voie a une participation de l'Algerie a des operations exterieures dans certaines conditions. Son article 31 prevoit que le pays peut contribuer au maintien de la paix, dans le respect des principes et des objectifs des Nations unies, de l'Union africaine et de la Ligue des etats arabes. L'article 91 encadre, pour sa part, les conditions dans lesquelles le president de la Republique peut decider de l'envoi d'unites de l'Armee nationale populaire a l'etranger, notamment apres approbation des deux tiers de chaque chambre du Parlement. L'approbation annoncee par le Conseil de la nation constitue donc une etape du processus institutionnel. Le vote de l'Assemblee populaire nationale et les modalites precises d'un eventuel deploiement restent determinants pour la suite de cette initiative.

items.title: How Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites deepened the rift with Trump
items.description: Relations between United States President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky took a sharp downward turn in recent weeks, with each leader openly criticising the other. The two have long had a testy relationship, but Trump’s frustration over Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure triggered a crisis that Kyiv’s supporters fear could threaten vital US support going forward. Here’s how the relationship soured: What is the history of Trump-Zelensky tensions? Trump has been skeptical of US involvement in Ukraine ever since his first term when, shortly after taking office in early 2017, he was asked to provide lethal aid to Ukraine and approved the sale of Javelin missiles to Kyiv. “Everyone around him wanted him to do it, and they pushed him hard and he eventually signed off on selling them Javelins, very reluctantly,” said a former senior Trump administration official, who spoke on condition of anonymity. “He didn’t consider it a core US interest. It was a European issue.” Trump’s first major encounter with Zelensky came in a July 2019 phone call in which the Republican president asked the Ukrainian leader to investigate his Democratic rival Joe Biden and his son Hunter, in exchange for military support Congress had authorised. That episode led to Trump’s first impeachment . Biden beat Trump in the 2020 presidential election. Trump also has fostered a relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin that runs against the norms of US foreign policy but echoes his warm ties with authoritarian leaders Xi Jinping of China and North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un. “Trump has always wanted better relations with Russia,” the former official said. What deepened the rift between the two leaders? Trump’s current frustration centres on Kyiv’s attacks on Russian diesel infrastructure. Diesel prices have hit record highs since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, and global energy costs spiked. US lawmakers in Trump’s Republican party face voter anger over inflation ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections . On Sept 13, Trump began publicly calling on Ukraine to stop targeting diesel infrastructure. The following week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was also concerned that Ukraine had hit US-linked oil shipments. Ukraine has refused to halt the strikes, saying its long-range drone campaign is its only viable response to nearly five years of Russian bombardment. Moscow was forced in July to ban diesel exports as part of a raft of measures to address domestic fuel shortages. Angered by Zelensky’s defiance, Trump on Oct 9 announced a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, issuing a temporary general license that allows Russian diesel to reach the global market. He also waived sanctions on Russia authorised by a bill he signed into law in September. Suriya Jayanti, a former US official who runs a power sector company in Ukraine, said Russia’s strikes on Ukraine’s power grid have increased, despite Trump unilaterally announcing an energy ceasefire on Oct 11. “It is clear to everyone in Kyiv that the goal is not actually an energy ceasefire, but it is really just an effort to hobble Ukraine and give Russia a decisive advantage,” said Jayanti, who is also a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council think tank. Has the US threatened to cut off support to Ukraine? Zelensky has said Ukrainian military officials had been threatened by US counterparts, who said continuing the energy strikes would lead the US to cut off intelligence sharing. A US official familiar with the situation disputed Kyiv’s account. Speaking on condition of anonymity, the US official said there has been no increase in pressure on Ukraine. We don’t have to pressure Zelensky. If he wants to make a deal he’ll make a deal. I think Putin is putting a ton of pressure on him and he (Zelensky) is putting some pressure on Russia but Russia doesn’t seem to be minding it as much even though they are getting hit.” On Thursday, Trump said he had asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to restore Ukraine’s access to the company’s Starlink satellite system. Starlink’s disruption temporarily hampered Kyiv’s military drone operations and spurred fears that Kyiv would be left defenceless against Russia’s attacks going into the winter. What is the status of Moscow-Kyiv peace talks? Peace efforts have continued but so far have not yielded tangible results. At talks in Oslo on October 20, Ukraine presented new proposals, and Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner repeated Trump’s demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian diesel refineries. The next day, envoy Witkoff — a close friend of Trump’s — met Putin in St. Petersburg. Putin agreed to release detained American Stephen Hubbard in what the two countries called a goodwill gesture. Zelensky said on Friday that negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US would meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, a possible precursor to a meeting of the three countries’ leaders. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February.

items.title: TOR eyes stock market listing as it tackles $517m debt
items.description: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) is considering a listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange as management seeks fresh investment while pursuing the restructuring of an inherited debt burden of approximately $517 million. Managing Director Edmond Kombat disclosed this during a visit by an International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation led by the Fund’s Ghana Resident Representative, Dr Adrian Alter. The delegation visited the refinery to assess rehabilitation works and understand efforts to restore sustained operations and financial stability. The engagement formed part of the IMF team’s discussions with government authorities and selected state-owned enterprises. Mr Kombat said a potential stock market listing would let Ghanaian institutions and other investors buy shares in TOR, providing capital for operations and expansion. He told the delegation that management had relied on internally generated funds since taking office in May 2025. “Since this new management took over, we have not received a dime from government. Every single thing is done through our internally generated funds,” he said. Mr Kombat said management had prioritised financial discipline, operational improvements and the rehabilitation of critical facilities. Of the approximately $517 million debt inherited, he said about $120 million was owed to the government. Discussions were underway to restructure that obligation and reconcile historical financial commitments between TOR and the state. The refinery is also engaging other state institutions over outstanding obligations. The refinery is exploring possible arrangements to offset amounts owed between the parties and establish their respective financial positions. Despite the debt burden, Mr Kombat said TOR recorded a profit last year. He expressed optimism that improved macroeconomic conditions and operational reforms would help sustain profitability. Responding to questions about crude supplies, he said the refinery had processed approximately five million barrels, including about two million barrels sourced from Ghana’s oil fields. The remainder came from external sources. “Our first domestic crude came from the Jubilee field through Vitol, and it was fully paid for. GNPC also gave us its portion of Ghana’s allocation,” he said. Mr Kombat expressed hope that the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation would make its full crude allocation available to TOR for refining by the following year. He said this would improve feedstock availability and support more consistent operations. He argued that domestic refining could strengthen petroleum supplies and reduce Ghana’s exposure to international market disruptions. Beyond refining, Mr Kombat highlighted opportunities to earn revenue from TOR’s storage infrastructure, distribution network and petroleum-testing laboratory. He said the refinery had approximately one million metric tonnes of storage capacity and connections to eight privately operated depots, allowing products to be pumped directly to those facilities. The discussions also addressed financial accountability, including efforts to clear a six-year backlog of unaudited accounts. Mr Kombat said the Ghana Audit Service had undertaken an audit exercise to address the backlog. Management also intended to appoint an external audit firm at the refinery’s next Annual General Meeting to handle subsequent audits. He outlined improvements to financial reporting, internal controls, and staff-related reforms, along with efforts to secure reliable crude supplies. The IMF delegation later toured rehabilitated facilities and ongoing engineering works. Management said the work aimed to improve processing capacity, restore critical units, and strengthen TOR’s contribution to Ghana’s energy security.

items.title: Students across country to get 500,000 Chromebooks over 2 years, announces PM Shehbaz
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday launched a scheme under which the government would distribute 500,000 Chromebook laptops to students nationwide over two years. He addressed the launch ceremony in Islamabad of the Prime Minister’s Youth Chromebook Scheme, a nationwide initiative to distribute 500,000 Chromebooks equipped with MiFi internet connectivity to deserving students and high achievers. Banners visible at the ceremony read “500,000 refurbished Chromebooks” were to be handed out. Expressing confidence in the initiative’s broad impact, the prime minister noted that the scheme’s internet connectivity features will extend benefits to family members, ultimately reaching an estimated 2.5 million people. He highlighted that the facility was available to students of religious seminaries, noting that previous laptop schemes had also successfully reached prominent religious seminaries. The prime minister stressed that the 500,000 Chromebooks will be distributed on the basis of the youth’s “ability and ability alone”. “These Chromebooks will help you gain further education, and in the future, these devices will help you secure employment,” the premier said. PM Shehbaz recalled that the previous PML-N governments distributed 600,000 laptops within a decade; however, he vowed that the government now aimed to distribute 500,000 Chromebooks in the next two years. “These wonderful instruments will be in your hands so that you are not lagging in intelligence and skills,” he said, stressing that intelligence and hard work should not be limited by poverty. The prime minister stressed that empowering the nation’s youth with modern tools was vital to helping them compete globally, while expressing gratitude to Tokyo Technology Care Foundation (TTCF) for partnering in the Chromebook initiative. At the outset of his address, the premier stressed that it was his duty and the state’s “collective responsibility” to provide the youth with modern technology, so they could become “the great builders of Pakistan”. “Our boys and girls [..] are the true assets of Pakistan,” the prime minister remarked. He added that the Chromebooks were being distributed based on the youth’s hard work and ability. He hoped students would be able to “attend school remotely [..] and find themselves amongst the most educated people” with the help of the device. Recalling the recent inauguration of a Daanish School in Islamabad, PM Shehbaz stressed that education “should be the priority of any government”. “For the development of the nation’s children, all the resources should be provided,” he said. “Education is a jewel; regardless of where you are from, it will always make you distinguished in society,” he remarked. The event was attended by ministers, parliamentarians, the Punjab Assembly speaker, educationists, vice chancellors, ambassadors and foreign guests. Ministers hail inclusion of seminary students Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif particularly highlighted the inclusion of seminary students in the scheme. In a post on X, Dar said, “Including madrasa students marks a historic national consensus that every child deserves the tools of the modern world.” Asif said that “madressah students were kept away from the mainstream for years”. He stated that one out of every five Chromebooks will be given to a student of a registered seminary under the new scheme. Addressing the Chromebook distribution ceremony, Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui emphasised that the government was striving to elevate Pakistan’s global standing by adapting to evolving educational trends. He noted that transforming the country’s 150 million youth into a productive national asset was crucial to ensuring the youth demographic drives progress rather than becoming a challenge. TTCF Chairman Rashid Minhas also spoke about the partnership, noting that the memorandum signed with the government aims to empower students to become creators in the digital world and spur a national digital revolution. Meanwhile, PM’s Youth Programme Chairman Rana Mashhood Ahmad Khan praised the prime minister’s vision for recognising young talent with the support of the overseas diaspora. In August, PM Shehbaz, speaking on the occasion of International Youth Day, said that 250,000 high-achieving students would be awarded Chromebook laptops this year. Last year, Pakistan launched its first Google Chromebook assembly line and hailed it as a “historic milestone” that would make digital tools more accessible. At the time, Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar had said the assembly line’s establishment held great economic significance as it laid the “foundation for jobs, supply chain, development and future tech exports”.

items.title: FEC : les financements territoriaux accélèrent, la mobilité urbaine en tête
items.description: Le Fonds d’Equipement Communal (FEC) a nettement renforcé son activité de financement au premier semestre 2026. Les engagements de prêts ont atteint 2,27 milliards de dirhams, en hausse de 46% sur un an, tandis que les décaissements ont progressé de 57%, à 1,41 milliard de dirhams. Derrière cette accélération, un changement marqué dans la composition des financements : la mobilité urbaine et interurbaine s’impose comme le principal moteur des engagements, alors que les aménagements urbains et les infrastructures routières concentrent l’essentiel des montants effectivement décaissés. Au terme des six premiers mois de l’année, le FEC a engagé 2.270 millions de dirhams au profit de 23 collectivités territoriales, pour 28 projets couvrant neuf secteurs d’intervention. Cette progression intervient dans un environnement marqué par l’intensification des investissements territoriaux et par la mise en œuvre de programmes consacrés à la mobilité urbaine et interurbaine. Le mouvement est particulièrement visible dans la ventilation sectorielle. Les engagements consacrés au transport urbain ont atteint 1,264 milliard de dirhams, contre seulement 80 millions un an auparavant. Leur poids dans le portefeuille d’engagements est ainsi passé de 5,1% au premier semestre 2025 à près de 56% à fin juin 2026. Le FEC explique cette évolution par le financement de programmes régionaux liés à la mise en œuvre du nouveau modèle de gestion déléguée du transport par autobus en milieu urbain et interurbain, avec notamment la modernisation des flottes et l’amélioration de la qualité des services. Cette concentration des nouveaux engagements autour de la mobilité ne signifie pas pour autant un recul des autres composantes de l’investissement territorial. Les infrastructures routières ont mobilisé 423 millions de dirhams, soit 18,6% du total, tandis que les aménagements urbains ont représenté 365 millions de dirhams, soit 16%. Au total, ces trois secteurs ont absorbé plus de 90% des prêts engagés au cours du semestre. Une autre lecture du semestre ressort des décaissements, qui donnent une image plus directe de la concrétisation des financements. Leur montant a atteint 1,413 milliard de dirhams, contre 900 millions au premier semestre 2025. Ces ressources ont permis au FEC de participer au financement de 49 projets au profit de 27 collectivités territoriales, couvrant huit secteurs. Les opérations concernent notamment des programmes de développement urbain et régional, le Programme de Réduction des Disparités Territoriales et Sociales ainsi que les investissements consacrés à la mobilité. La structure des décaissements révèle toutefois une hiérarchie différente de celle observée au niveau des engagements. Les aménagements urbains arrivent en tête avec 528 millions de dirhams, soit 37% du total. Ils sont suivis par les infrastructures routières, avec 458 millions de dirhams et une part de 32%, puis par le transport urbain, avec 264 millions de dirhams, soit 19%. Ces trois postes représentent ainsi plus de 88% des décaissements réalisés au premier semestre. Cette répartition traduit la diversité des investissements accompagnés par le FEC. Les financements consacrés aux aménagements urbains portent notamment sur les voiries et places publiques, la mise à niveau des infrastructures de base et la restructuration de quartiers sous-équipés. Les concours destinés au réseau routier concernent, de leur côté, la construction de liaisons et d’ouvrages d’art, notamment dans le cadre du PRDTS, ainsi que l’aménagement de voies rapides destinées à fluidifier la circulation dans les grandes agglomérations. Le volet transport accompagne, pour sa part, le nouveau modèle de gestion déléguée du transport par autobus. Le poids des Conseils Régionaux confirme également le rôle croissant de l’échelon régional dans la programmation des investissements. Ils ont concentré 1,878 milliard de dirhams, soit près de 83% des engagements du semestre. Les Conseils Communaux ont représenté environ 15%, avec 338 millions de dirhams, tandis que les Conseils Préfectoraux et Provinciaux ont bénéficié de 54 millions, soit 2%. Sur le plan financier, cette forte progression de l’activité de crédit ne s’est pas traduite par une hausse du produit net bancaire. Celui-ci s’est établi à 326 millions de dirhams, quasiment au même niveau que les 328 millions enregistrés un an auparavant. Le FEC explique cette stabilité par l’effet de la baisse des taux appliqués aux prêts accordés aux collectivités territoriales, partiellement compensé par l’augmentation des volumes financés. Les produits d’exploitation bancaire ont ainsi reculé de 5%, à 704 millions de dirhams, tandis que les charges d’exploitation bancaire ont diminué de 8%, à 378 millions. L’amélioration du coût des ressources a joué un rôle dans cet équilibre. Le coût moyen du stock des ressources est passé de 3,5% à fin juin 2025 à 3,2% un an plus tard, tandis que les charges d’exploitation bancaire ont diminué de 8%. Le FEC attribue notamment cette évolution à l’optimisation de la mobilisation des ressources, au recours aux financements auprès des institutions financières de développement et aux opérations de reengineering de la dette. La qualité du portefeuille constitue un autre élément marquant du semestre. Les créances en souffrance ont chuté de 149 millions à 30 millions de dirhams en un an, soit une baisse de 80%. Leur taux rapporté aux engagements est ainsi passé de 0,56% à 0,11%. Le FEC attribue cette évolution à sa gestion du risque de contrepartie et aux efforts de recouvrement. Le bilan reste dominé par l’activité de financement des collectivités territoriales. Les créances sur la clientèle ont atteint 27,2 milliards de dirhams à fin juin 2026, en progression de 2,8% sur un an et représentant 96% du total bilan. Les capitaux propres et assimilés se sont, pour leur part, établis à près de 6,9 milliards de dirhams. Cette montée en puissance de l’activité intervient alors que le FEC poursuit la diversification de ses ressources. Le financement international occupe une place croissante dans cette stratégie. En juillet 2026, la Banque Africaine de Développement a signé avec le FEC un deuxième accord de financement, d’un montant de 150 millions d’euros, après un premier accord de 100 millions d’euros conclu en mars 2024. La nouvelle ligne doit soutenir les programmes de développement et les projets d’investissement des collectivités territoriales. Elle est assortie d’un accord de don, d’une lettre d’intention et d’une assistance technique destinée à renforcer les capacités opérationnelles du FEC. Le modèle de financement du FEC reste particulier, l’établissement ne disposant pas de dépôts de clientèle. Ses ressources reposent notamment sur les recouvrements d’annuités, qui ont représenté 74% de ses ressources au premier semestre, ainsi que sur ses emprunts et ses partenariats avec les institutions financières de développement. Dans ce cadre, le FEC indique être engagé dans des discussions avancées avec d’autres bailleurs internationaux afin de renforcer et diversifier ses ressources. items.description: Francisco Martín Aguirre ha presentado su dimisión como delegado del Gobierno en la Comunidad de Madrid, cargo que ejercía desde marzo de 2023, han avanzado fuentes socialistas a EL PAÍS. El dirigente del PSOE ha justificado su renuncia con el argumento de que “no se dan las condiciones para seguir ejerciendo su responsabilidad”, según fuentes de la Delegación. items.title: Man United’s misery continues, suffer 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth
items.description: Manchester United slumped further into crisis with a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday that plunged Michael Carrick’s future as manager into doubt. Carrick’s bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United’s winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won 3-0 at Old Trafford as goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved win for Marco Rose’s side. Fernandes was critical of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como on Wednesday. The United boss said the decision to leave out last season’s Premier League player of the year was a “purely football” driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match. Carrick was taunted with chants of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” from the Bournemouth fans. But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago. A strong finish to last season during Carrick’s interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League, but was aided by a lack of European or domestic cup football. United have won just twice — against newly-promoted Ipswich and Azerbaijani side Sabah — in 12 games in all competitions this season. Bournemouth began the day behind the Red Devils in the table after a difficult start for Rose. But just three days after beating AC Milan 3-0, they outclassed another giant of the European game. Rayan opened the floodgates when he connected sweetly with Justin Kluivert’s free-kick on 38 minutes. Five minutes later, Leny Yoro stumbled under pressure from Adrien Truffert and the French full-back had a simple task to square for Tavernier to tap into an empty net. Many expected Fernandes to be stripped and ready for the start of the second half, but he remained on the bench and the United performance got no better. Inside the first minute of the restart Evanilson found the net, but was flagged offside. That let-off mattered little as Bournemouth could have run out even more convincing winners. Senne Lammens denied Rayan before the Brazilian winger fired wide after racing past Lisandro Martinez. Evanilson did finally add a third 20 minutes from time when he rounded Lammens before curling in an exquisite finish from a narrow angle. The United support unleashed their fury at the club’s unpopular owners, the Glazer family, rather than Carrick in the closing stages. Carrick applauded the Stretford End and touched his chest as he made his way down the tunnel. However, it is the manager who will likely be the fall guy after another miserable afternoon for the 20-time English champions. items.title: Kaylia Nemour, en or, prend sa revanche sur la Chinoise Zhang à Rotterdam
items.description: Et de deux pour Kaylia Nemour ! La championne olympique algérienne a ajouté une deuxième médaille d’or aux championnats du monde 2026 qui se déroulent à Rotterdam (Pays-Bas). La gymnaste de 19 ans s’est imposée ce dimanche 25 octobre au concours de la poutre, au lendemain de sa victoire aux barres asymétriques. Après les barres asymétriques, Kaylia Nemour championne du monde de la poutre Kaylia Nemour a remporté l’épreuve de la poutre avec un score de 14.566 points, en s’imposant au bout du suspense devant la Chinoise Qinqying Zhang, qui a réalisé le même score, mais avec une exécution inférieure, et la Brésilienne Flavia Saraiva (14.300 points). La Chinoise Zhang perd son titre remporté à Jakarta en octobre 2025 où Kaylia Nemour avait gagné la médaille d’argent. À Rotterdam, l’Algérienne a pris sa revanche. Samedi, l'Algérienne s'est imposée sans surprise dans son agrès de prédilection, les barres asymétriques, avec une note de 15.333. تهانيّ الحارّة كيليا..سعيد وفخور بكِ، مثل كل الجزائريين لهذا التتويج المزدوج بالذهب، في بطولة العالم للجمباز الفني، بهولندا..تستحقين على الدوام كل التقدير لتشريفك راية الوطن..تحيا الجزائر — عبدالمجيد تبون – Abdelmadjid Tebboune (@TebbouneAmadjid) October 25, 2026 Troisième médaille d’or pour Kaylia Nemour depuis 2025 La médaille d’or remportée ce dimanche est la deuxième pour la championne algérienne dans ce tournoi et la troisième pour elle en championnats du monde après celle décrochée en 2025 à Jakarta (Indonésie). À Rotterdam, Kaylia Nemour a aussi terminé au pied du podium (4e) au concours général, remporté vendredi 23 octobre par l’Américaine Blakely Skye. Cet échec n’a pas pesé sur le moral de l’Algérienne qui a enchaîné deux médailles d’or pour la première fois aux championnats du monde de gymnastique. En octobre 2025 à Jakara, elle s’était imposée sur les barres asymétriques, l’agrès où elle écrase la concurennce. Championne olympique en 2024 à Paris, Kaylia Nemour a dans le viseur les Jeux olympiques 2028 de Los Angeles. items.title: Ebola: NCDC tracks 53 contacts, orders hospitals to isolate suspects
items.description: Patient improves as DG warns against delayed precautions Rivers suspected case tests negative By Chioma Obinna & Chidinma Chukwu The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has identified 53 contacts of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola patient for follow-up and directed hospitals nationwide to promptly isolate suspected cases without waiting for laboratory confirmation, as authorities intensify efforts to contain the outbreak. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, gave the directive following confirmation of Ebola Disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, on October 20, warning that prompt identification of suspected cases and strict infection prevention measures were critical to protecting healthcare workers and preventing further transmission. The patient, a 42-year-old woman who returned to Nigeria from Uganda through Addis Ababa on October 3, was reported to have improved remarkably while receiving care in isolation, according to the NCDC’s Ebola Disease Situation Report dated October 24. The 53 contacts identified by the response team include healthcare workers, domestic staff and the patient’s spouse. They have been categorised and are being followed up, with monitoring to continue for 21 days after their last possible exposure. The NCDC said contact tracing remained a priority in the response, as public health teams worked to identify and monitor people who may have been exposed to the confirmed case. Idris said the detection of the case demonstrated the importance of surveillance systems and the vigilance of healthcare workers. “The detection of this case demonstrates the importance of the surveillance systems we have continued to strengthen over the years,” he said. He stressed that hospitals must not wait for laboratory confirmation before taking precautions when Ebola is suspected. “Any suspected case must be promptly separated from other patients and reported to the relevant public health authorities. Healthcare workers should not wait for laboratory confirmation before taking appropriate precautions,” the NCDC boss said. He also emphasised the need to protect health workers, who are at risk of exposure when suspected cases are not promptly recognised and managed. “Protecting healthcare workers is essential to protecting the communities they serve,” Idris said. The confirmed case followed an alert from a private health facility on October 19. According to the situation report, the woman developed symptoms on October 7, four days after arriving in Nigeria. Her symptoms included fever, diarrhoea, generalised body aches and sore throat. She presented at a private health facility on October 10 and was admitted to another private facility on October 11. The NCDC was notified on October 19, and laboratory testing confirmed the infection the following day. No bleeding was reported in the case details contained in the situation report. Following confirmation, the NCDC activated its national incident management system at the highest level, with response activities coordinated through the Emergency Operations Centre in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, FCT authorities and partners. The response includes surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory investigations, infection prevention and control, risk communication and measures to strengthen preparedness across health facilities. The agency said hospitals should maintain effective screening and triage systems, promptly separate suspected cases from other patients, notify public health authorities and apply appropriate infection prevention and control precautions. These measures include hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, injection safety, safe handling of sharps, proper waste management and the appropriate use of personal protective equipment. The NCDC’s warning is directed at preventing delays that could expose other patients, healthcare workers and caregivers before a suspected infection is recognised and the necessary precautions are implemented. In a related development, a suspected Ebola case reported in Rivers State on October 23 tested negative, according to the NCDC’s situation report. The negative result meant the Rivers alert had not resulted in another confirmed case in the report. However, surveillance and investigation of suspected cases remain important components of the response. The NCDC also emphasised the importance of cooperation from people identified as contacts, cautioning against stigma and misinformation. “Being identified as a contact does not mean that you have Ebola,” Idris said. The agency urged the public to rely on official information and cooperate with public health teams carrying out contact tracing and follow-up. Idris warned that misinformation could undermine containment efforts by creating fear and discouraging people from reporting symptoms. “False information can create fear, discourage people from reporting symptoms and undermine the cooperation essential to stopping transmission,” he said. He recalled Nigeria’s experience in containing the 2014 Ebola outbreak, noting that lessons from that response were informing current preparedness and containment efforts. As part of investigations into the confirmed case, genomic sequencing was completed by the NCDC’s National Reference Laboratory and the African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases. The sequencing formed part of the laboratory work being undertaken alongside contact tracing and other response activities. The NCDC said prompt reporting of suspected cases, effective surveillance, timely isolation and strict infection prevention measures remained central to the effort to contain the confirmed case and detect any further infections. The agency’s directive to hospitals is that suspected cases must be separated from other patients and reported promptly, with protective measures implemented before laboratory results are available. Idris said protecting healthcare workers and maintaining public cooperation were essential to the response, as authorities continued to monitor contacts and strengthen measures aimed at preventing further transmission.
